definition_zh: 词汇学
definition_en: the branch of linguistics that studies the words of a language, including their forms, meanings, and relations to one another
core_image: 一整面墙的词语被摊在实验台上，放大镜一格格检视每个词的结构与关系
scene: 研究生的论文要写颜色词，导师建议先去修词汇学，把词的搭配和意义演变理清楚。A postgraduate wanted to write about colour words, and her supervisor told her to take a course in lexicology first so that she could sort out their combinations and shifts in meaning.
sceneCN: 这里 lexicology 是「词汇学」（第 1 个义项：研究语言词汇的学科）；句意：一位研究生想写颜色词，导师让她先修一门词汇学，好理清颜色词的搭配与意义演变。

pos.zh: 词汇学

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「词汇学的」
把 -logy 换成表示人的 -logist，义为「词汇学家」
同一词干换用 -graphy（书写）构成，义为「词典编纂」，属应用工作是词汇学的邻居
同一词干的名词原形，义为「词汇总集；词典」
加形容词词尾 -al 构成，义为「词汇的」，是这门学科常用的属性形容词

senses.title: The study of vocabulary
senses.titleCN: 词汇学：研究语言词汇的学科
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that examines the words of a language, their structure, and their place in the system
senses.definitionCN: 语言学的一个分支，考察一种语言的词语、其结构以及在语言系统中的地位
senses.example: Lexicology asks why some words are stored as single units and others as phrases.
senses.exampleCN: 词汇学要追问：为什么有些词被当作单个单位储存，有些却当作短语。
senses.why: Greek lexis names words and -logia names a field of study, so lexicology is the discipline that takes the word store itself as its object.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 lexis 指词语，-logia 指研究领域，所以词汇学就是把「词语库存」本身当研究对象的学问。

senses.title: Study of word meaning and sense relations
senses.titleCN: 词义与语义关系的研究
senses.definition: the study of what words mean and how senses relate through synonymy, opposition, and inclusion
senses.definitionCN: 研究词语的意义，以及同义、反义、上下位等意义关系
senses.example: Lexicology maps how the sense of a word can split into several related senses.
senses.exampleCN: 词汇学描绘一个词的意义如何分裂成几个相关的义项。
senses.why: Once words are gathered on the table, the first thing to compare is their meaning, so this branch grows out of the central question of what a word carries.
senses.whyCN: 词语一旦被摊到台面上，第一件要做的事就是比较意义，于是这一分支从「词到底承载什么」这个核心问题里长出来。

senses.title: Study of word formation
senses.definition: the study of how new words are coined, borrowed, or built from prefixes, suffixes, and compounds
senses.definitionCN: 研究新词如何被创造、借用，或由前缀、后缀、复合构成
senses.example: Work in lexicology shows how blog gave rise to blogging and blogger.
senses.exampleCN: 词汇学的研究显示 blog 如何衍生出 blogging 与 blogger。
senses.why: If the lexicon is a growing collection, the science must explain where new pieces come from, which turns attention to word formation.
senses.whyCN: 既然词汇是一份不断扩充的收藏，这门学问就必须解释新藏品从哪儿来，注意力于是转向构词法。

senses.title: Historical lexicology
senses.definition: the study of how the vocabulary of a language changed over time, including borrowings and semantic shifts
senses.definitionCN: 研究一种语言的词汇随时间如何变化，包括借词与意义演变
senses.example: Historical lexicology traces the shift of nice from foolish to pleasant.
senses.exampleCN: 历史词汇学追踪 nice 从「愚蠢」到「令人愉快」的演变。
senses.why: Meaning changes are evidence of a moving system, so a science of words naturally splits into a synchronic and a diachronic side.
senses.whyCN: 意义会变化，说明词汇系统在移动，于是这门词的科学自然分成共时与历时两支。

senses.title: A systematic way of comparing vocabulary
senses.definition: in broader use, a systematic method of examining and comparing the vocabulary of a subject or of several languages
senses.definitionCN: 在更宽泛的用法中，指系统检视、比较某领域或多种语言词汇的方法
senses.example: The essay offers a lexicology of climate language across three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章对三种语言里的气候用语做了一次词汇学式的比较。
senses.why: When the discipline is applied to a field instead of a whole language, the name stretches to mean the method rather than the branch of linguistics.
senses.whyCN: 当这门学科被用来研究某个领域而不是整门语言时，名称就从「语言学分支」扩展成了「一种方法」。

intro.en: Lexicology joins Greek lexis, speech or a word, and -logia, the study of a subject, and follows the pattern of earlier titles such as lexicography.
intro.cn: lexicology 由希腊语 lexis（言语、词）加 -logia（某学科的学问）构成，并沿用了 lexicography 等更早称谓的造词模式。

items.en: Legein gathers and speaks, and the noun lexis names speech, a phrase, or a single word.
items.cn: 希腊语 legein 兼有「收集」和「说出」之意，名词 lexis 指言语、说法或单个的词。

items.en: Logos means word, reason, and account, and the element -logia builds the names of learned disciplines.
items.cn: logos 意为词语、道理与论述，构词成分 -logia 用来给各种学问命名。

items.en: The compound is formed on the model of lexicography, replacing the writing element with the study element.
items.cn: 这个复合词依照 lexicography 的模式而造成，把「书写」那一部分换成了「研究」那一部分。

items.en: The French term lexicologie appears in the nineteenth century as linguistics develops as a discipline.
items.cn: 随着语言学逐渐成为一门学科，法语词 lexicologie 在十九世纪出现。

items.en: English takes lexicology in the middle of the nineteenth century to name the study of vocabulary.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中叶吸收 lexicology，用它指对词汇的研究。

items.en: In the twentieth century the term firms up in contrast with lexicography, the practical work of making dictionaries.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词与「编词典」的实务 lexicography 明确区分开来，固定为学科名。

note.en: Lexicology is one of many -logy titles and is often confused with lexicography, so a careful learner keeps the study of words apart from the making of dictionaries.
note.cn: lexicology 是众多 -logy 学科名之一，常与 lexicography 混淆，所以细心的学习者会把「研究词语」与「编写词典」分开。

entries.definition: a person who studies lexicology
entries.definitionCN: 词汇学家

entries.definition: the practice or study of making dictionaries
entries.definitionCN: 词典编纂；词典学（同一词干，后缀不同）

entries.definition: relating to the study of vocabulary
entries.definitionCN: 词汇学的

entries.definition: the study of meaning in language
entries.definitionCN: 语义学的范围更宽，涵盖句子与意义

entries.definition: the study of the structure of words
entries.definitionCN: 形态学：研究词的内部结构，是词汇学的近邻

entries.definition: the study of the origin and history of words
entries.definitionCN: 词源学：研究词语的来源与历史

normalIntro.en: Lexicology is lexis plus -logy, the words of a language plus the study of them, and every hook that links it to the -logy family of subjects will keep the meaning steady.
normalIntro.cn: lexicology 是 lexis 加 -logy，即「一门语言的词语」加「对它的研究」，任何把它和 -logy 家族学科联系起来的钩子都能稳住意思。

normal.en: The ending -logy comes from Greek logos and appears in biology, psychology, and many other subject names.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 来自希腊语 logos，也出现在 biology、psychology 等许多学科名里。

normal.en: Lexis means the total stock of words, so lexicology is the study of exactly that stock.
normal.cn: lexis 意为词语的总和，所以词汇学研究的正是这份总和。

normal.en: Keep lexicology apart from lexicography: one studies words, the other compiles them into a dictionary.
normal.cn: 把词汇学与 lexicography 分开：一个研究词，另一个把词汇编成词典。

normal.en: Chinese learners often meet lexicology in the phrase English lexicology, a standard course name.
normal.cn: 中国学习者常在「英语词汇学」这个标准课程名里遇到 lexicology。

normal.en: The word stresses the syllable before -logy, so it sounds like lex-i-COL-o-gy.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -logy 前面那个音节上，读起来像 lex-i-COL-o-gy。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of words laid out on a bench under a magnifying glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面墙的词语被摆到工作台上，有一把放大镜依次检视它们。

abstract.en: Imagine sorting thousands of words into boxes marked same meaning, opposite meaning, and part of.
abstract.cn: 想象把上千个词分别放进「同义」「反义」「上下位」几个盒子。

abstract.en: Think of a family tree in which each new word is a child of an older one.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家族树，每个新词都是某个老词的孩子。

examples.en: The textbook introduces English lexicology through word formation and sense relations.
examples.cn: 这本教材通过构词与语义关系来介绍英语词汇学。

examples.en: She turned from lexicology to lexicography and joined a dictionary team.
examples.cn: 她从词汇学转向词典编纂，加入了一个词典编写团队。

examples.en: Historical lexicology shows that borrowed words rarely keep their original meaning.
examples.cn: 历史词汇学表明，借来的词很少能保持原义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克西瞎了去」：一位老师把词一条条「来克」，把孩子们弄「瞎了去」似的翻遍词典，只为讲清楚词——这就是词汇学。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 legein（收集、说话）与 lexis（言辞、词）→ 拉丁语 lexicon（词语之书）→ 词干 lexic- 加希腊语 -logia（学问）→ 英语 lexicology，核心义「对词语的研究」。

sensesIntro.en: Lexicology opens as the discipline of vocabulary as a system, then narrows to meaning and sense relations, then to word formation, then to the historical side, and finally stretches to any systematic comparison of a vocabulary.
sensesIntro.cn: lexicology 先指把词汇当作系统来研究的学科，再收窄到词义与语义关系，然后指构词，接着指历时研究，最后扩展到对某套词汇所做的系统比较。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of words examined one by one under a magnifying glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整面墙的词语在放大镜下被逐一检视。

branches.en: The central sense is vocabulary as a system under study.
branches.cn: 中心义项是把词汇当作系统来研究。

branches.en: Meaning and sense relations are the first layer of that system.
branches.cn: 意义与语义关系是这个系统的第一层。

branches.en: Word formation explains how the system grows.
branches.cn: 构词解释这个系统如何生长。

branches.en: Historical study adds time to the picture.
branches.cn: 历时研究为这幅图加上时间维度。

branches.en: A whole discipline and a comparison method both rest on the same idea of treating words as evidence.
branches.cn: 整门学科与一种比较方法，都建立在「把词语当作证据」这同一个想法上。

intro.en: Lexicology joins the stem lexic-, from Greek lexikon, to the Greek combining form -logy, and the same stem also builds lexical, lexicon, and lexicography.
intro.cn: lexicology 由词干 lexic-（来自希腊语 lexikon）加希腊语构词成分 -logy 构成，同一词干还组成 lexical、lexicon 与 lexicography。

latinIntro.en: Greek lexis means speech or a word, legein means to gather and to speak, and logos gives the -logy ending that means a field of study.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 lexis 意为言语或词，legein 意为收集、说话，logos 提供表示「研究领域」的词尾 -logy。

items.example: The stem lexic- supplies the object of study.
items.exampleCN: 词干 lexic- 提供研究对象。

items.example: The suffix -logy turns the stem into a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logy 把词干变成一门学科。

items.example: The ending -logist names the specialist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logist 指这门学问的专家。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms lexicological.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ical 构成 lexicological。

items.example: Lexicography is the sister term built on writing.
items.exampleCN: lexicography 是建立于「书写」之上的姊妹词。

items.meaning: the vocabulary of a language, a dictionary
items.example: Lexicon is the noun that lexicology studies.
items.exampleCN: lexicon 正是词汇学研究的对象。

items.example: Biology shows the same -logy ending at work.
items.exampleCN: biology 展示了同一个 -logy 词尾的用法。

items.example: The lexicologist compares the colour terms of two languages.
items.exampleCN: 这位词汇学家比较两种语言的颜色词。

definition_zh: 联络；联系；联络人；私通；（词间）连读
definition_en: communication or a working connection between groups, or a person who arranges it
core_image: 两座楼之间架起的一座窄桥，桥上来回传递消息的人
scene: 机场里翻译被雇来搭起两边的桥梁，让旅客与海关顺畅沟通。At the airport a translator was hired as a liaison between the passengers and the customs officers.
sceneCN: 这里 liaison 是「联络、联络人」（第 1 个义项：团体之间的沟通与联络）；句意：机场请来一位翻译，作为旅客与海关之间的联络人。

pos.zh: 联络；联系；联络人
私通；非法联系

derivatives.zh: 由 liaison 去掉词尾名词后缀反构出的动词，义为「联络；建立合作」
liaison 加动名词词尾构成的临时名词，义为「从事联络工作」
由 liaison 与 officer 组成的复合名词，专职联络的官员

senses.title: Communication between groups
senses.definition: the working communication that keeps two groups, units, or people in touch
senses.definitionCN: 使两个团体、单位或个人保持联系的工作性沟通
senses.example: There is close liaison between the hospital and the fire service.
senses.exampleCN: 医院与消防部门之间保持着密切联系。
senses.why: The French root meant a binding or a bond, so liaison is the bond that keeps separate groups joined.
senses.whyCN: 法语词根意为「捆绑、联结」，因此 liaison 就是把分开的团体系在一起的那根纽带。

senses.title: The person who links groups
senses.definition: a person whose job is to carry messages and keep cooperation between two sides
senses.definitionCN: 专职传递消息、维持双方合作的人
senses.example: She works as a liaison officer for the police.
senses.exampleCN: 她给警方当联络官。
senses.why: Once the bond between groups is a recognised role, the person who holds that bond can be called a liaison.
senses.whyCN: 当团体之间的纽带变成一个正式职位时，维系这条纽带的人就被称为 liaison。

senses.title: A secret love affair
senses.definition: an often secret sexual or romantic relationship, especially one that causes scandal
senses.definitionCN: 常指隐秘的性关系或恋情，尤指会引起丑闻的那种
senses.example: The novel is about a secret liaison between a soldier and a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说讲一名士兵跟护士之间的秘密恋情。
senses.why: A private joining of two lives is also a kind of bond, so the word drifted from political bonds to lovers ties.
senses.whyCN: 两个人私下结合也是一种「捆绑」，于是这个词从政治联盟滑向了男女私情。

senses.title: A thickening in cooking
senses.definition: a cooked mixture, often of egg yolks and cream, used to thicken soups and sauces
senses.definitionCN: 由蛋黄与奶油等调成、用来使汤和酱汁变稠的混合物
senses.example: Add the egg and cream liaison just before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前再加入蛋黄奶油稠化剂。
senses.why: In the kitchen the liaison binds liquid and fat together, the same binding image moved to food.
senses.whyCN: 在厨房里，liaison 把液体和油脂「绑」在一起，仍是同一个捆绑意象。

senses.title: A joining in phonetics
senses.definition: the pronunciation of a silent final consonant before a word that begins with a vowel
senses.definitionCN: 在元音开头的词前，把原本不发音的词尾辅音读出来的现象
senses.example: French learners practise liaison between words.
senses.exampleCN: 法语学习者练习词与词之间的连读。
senses.why: Two words are pronounced as if held together, so the word again describes a bond between separate things.
senses.whyCN: 两个词被连起来读，于是这个词又一次描述两个分开之物之间的联结。

intro.en: Liaison comes from the Latin verb ligare, to bind, through French lier and Middle French liasion.
intro.cn: liaison 源出拉丁语动词 ligare（捆、绑），经法语 lier 与中古法语 liasion 进入英语。

items.en: Ligare means to tie, to bind, and to unite.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆、绑、连接。

items.en: Ligatio names a binding or a tying together.
items.cn: ligatio 指一次捆绑的动作或纽带。

items.en: Lier carries the binding sense into French.
items.cn: lier 把这层「捆绑」带入法语。

items.en: Liasion is the linking together of parts.
items.cn: 中古法语 liasion 指若干部分被连在一起。

items.en: English adopts liaison for connections in policy and in cooking.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 liaison，先用于政治与烹饪中的连接。

items.en: The word later covers romantic secrets and word joining in speech.
items.cn: 此后这个词又扩展到秘密恋情以及语音上的连读。

note.en: Liaison is the bond that holds groups together, near liaise, and near words like connection and intermediary.
note.cn: liaison 是把团体系在一起的纽带，它与 liaise 同族，也靠近 connection、intermediary 这类表示「连接」的词。

entries.definition: to work with another group and keep communication open
entries.definitionCN: 与另一团体合作并保持沟通

entries.definition: a group of teams or countries that act together
entries.definitionCN: 联赛；联盟（与 ligare 同源）

entries.definition: legally responsible or likely to do something
entries.definitionCN: 有法律责任的；易于……的（与 ligare 同源）

entries.definition: a link between people or things
entries.definitionCN: 联系；关联

entries.definition: a person who passes messages between two sides
entries.definitionCN: 中间人；调解人

entries.definition: the act of working together towards a shared aim
entries.definitionCN: 合作

normalIntro.en: Liaison is the bridge rope of Latin ligare: two sides stay joined through it.
normalIntro.cn: liaison 是拉丁语 ligare 留下的绑绳：两边靠它系在一起。

normal.en: A liaison officer is the living rope between two offices.
normal.cn: liaison officer 就是两个办公室之间的活绳。

normal.en: In liaison with a partner means working with them closely.
normal.cn: in liaison with 表示与某人密切配合。

normal.en: Keep the silent s: liaison is chained to ligare, the tying verb.
normal.cn: 记住那个不发音的 s：liaison 与表示「捆绑」的 ligare 同根。

normal.en: Compare liaison with liable and league, all from the binding root.
normal.cn: 对比 liaison、liable 与 league，它们都出自「捆绑」这一词根。

normal.en: A love liaison is the word binding two private lives.
normal.cn: 爱情中的 liaison 是把两段私生活绑在一起的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a messenger running back and forth across a thin bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一位信使在窄桥上来回奔跑。

abstract.en: See one person holding both ends of a telephone cord.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人手握着电话线的两头。

abstract.en: Imagine two hands secretly tied by a red thread.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手被一根红线悄悄系在一起。

examples.en: The school appointed her as liaison between teachers and parents.
examples.cn: 学校任命她担任教师与家长之间的联络人。

examples.en: Our teams work in close liaison during every project.
examples.cn: 我们的团队在每个项目中都保持密切联络。

examples.en: The scandal exposed a hidden liaison between two ministers.
examples.cn: 丑闻曝光了两位部长之间的隐秘私情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离爱身」——把「离」开的身心重新「爱」过来，牵起联络之线；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ligare（捆、绑）→ ligatio（捆绑）→ 法语 lier（连接）→ 中古法语 liasion → 英语 liaison，核心义「把分开的东西系在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: Liaison starts as a bond of communication, then names the person who holds that bond, and spreads to lovers and to speech.
sensesIntro.cn: liaison 先指沟通的纽带，再指维系列纽带的人，随后延伸到男女私情与语音连读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bridge that carries messages between two buildings.
core.cn: 核心意象：两座楼之间那条传递消息的窄桥。

branches.en: Open working communication is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 公开的工作沟通是日常义项。

branches.en: The link person is the role sense.
branches.cn: 联络人的职位是角色义项。

branches.en: Lovers and sauce thickeners are both private kinds of binding.
branches.cn: 恋人与浓稠剂都是私下、材料层面的「联结」。

branches.en: Word joining keeps the same image inside language.
branches.cn: 词间连读把同一意象带进了语言内部。

branches.en: A liaison officer exists so that liaison can happen.
branches.cn: 联络官的存在正是为了让联络发生。

intro.en: Liaison is built on the Latin binding verb ligare, with English liaise and liable in the same family.
intro.cn: liaison 建立在拉丁语表示「捆绑」的动词 ligare 之上，英语中 liaise 与 liable 也属于同一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ligare is to bind, and nouns such as ligatio and ligamen grow from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，ligatio、ligamen 等名词都由它构成。

items.example: Ligare supplies the binding picture.
items.exampleCN: ligare 提供捆绑的画面。

items.example: Ligatio is the closest Latin cousin.
items.exampleCN: ligatio 是最接近的拉丁同源词。

items.example: French lier carries the bond forward.
items.exampleCN: 法语 lier 把「联结」义继续传下。

items.example: Middle French liasion enters English.
items.exampleCN: 中古法语 liasion 进入英语。

items.meaning: to keep in touch and cooperate
items.example: Liaise means to establish liaison.
items.exampleCN: liaise 意为建立联络。

items.meaning: bound by law or likely to happen
items.meaningCN: 受法律约束的；易于发生的
items.example: Liable shares the binding root.
items.exampleCN: liable 共享「捆绑」词根。

items.example: League also descends from ligare.
items.exampleCN: league 同样源自 ligare。

items.meaning: a duty that binds a person
items.example: Obligation carries the prefix ob- onto the same root.
items.exampleCN: obligation 以 ob- 前缀接在同一词根上。

items.meaningCN: liaison 一词中的法语名词词尾
items.example: The son ending was later reduced.
items.exampleCN: 这个 son 词尾后来被简化。

definition_zh: 诽谤；文字诽谤；诽谤文字；对……提起诽谤诉讼
definition_en: a written or published statement that unfairly damages a person reputation, or the crime of making one
core_image: 一张印刷小册子被当众贴出，字句像墨点一样往人名上泼
scene: 报纸把商人写成骗子，结果被告上法庭。The newspaper printed that the shopkeeper was a cheat, and he sued it for libel.
sceneCN: 这里 libel 是「文字诽谤」（第 1 个义项：以书面或公开印刷的方式毁人名誉）；句意：报纸把这位店主写成骗子，于是店主以诽谤罪起诉了报社。

pos.zh: 诽谤；文字诽谤
诽谤性的文字
诽谤；以书面毁人名誉

derivatives.zh: libel 加形容词后缀成 -ous 构成，义为「诽谤性的」
libel 加 -ant 构成，指提起诽谤诉讼的人
libel 加动作执行者后缀 -er 构成，指诽谤他人的人

senses.title: Damage to reputation by writing
senses.definition: the legal wrong of publishing a false statement that harms a person reputation
senses.definitionCN: 以公开发表的方式散播不实说法、损伤他人名誉的法律过错
senses.example: He sued the magazine for libel.
senses.exampleCN: 他起诉那家杂志诽谤。
senses.why: The Latin source was libellus, a little book, so libel first meant a written statement that did damage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头 libellus 意为「小书」，所以 libel 最初就指造成损害的那种书面文字。

senses.title: The offensive publication itself
senses.definition: a specific written or printed statement that is claimed to be defamatory
senses.definitionCN: 被指为毁人名誉的具体书面或印刷文字
senses.example: The court found the article a libel on the mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭认定那篇文章是对市长的诽谤。
senses.why: From the abstract wrong the same noun came to name the concrete text that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 从抽象的法律过错出发，同一个名词也转指承载这过错的实体文字。

senses.title: To publish a defamatory statement
senses.definition: to publish something that wrongly damages a person reputation
senses.definitionCN: 公开刊布不实内容、毁损他人名誉
senses.example: The pamphlet libelled several local doctors.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子诽谤了当地好几位医生。
senses.why: Once the noun names the harm, English reuses it as a verb for the act of causing that harm.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指这种损害，英语便把它借作动词，表示施加这种损害的动作。

senses.title: An old church petition
senses.definition: in church law, an original written statement in which a plaintiff sets out a complaint
senses.definitionCN: 在教会法中，原告最初提交的书面控告
senses.example: The old records show a libel filed against the priest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案里有一条针对该神职人员的诉状。
senses.why: The little book of Roman law was a written claim, so in courts a libel could be the plaintiffs statement itself.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法中的「小书」本就是一份书面主张，因此在法庭上 libel 也可以指原告本人的诉状。

senses.title: Spoken slander counted as law
senses.definition: in some jurisdictions, any defamatory statement, written or spoken, sued for as a libel
senses.definitionCN: 在某些司法辖区里，无论书面还是口头的毁誉言论都以诽谤之名起诉
senses.example: In that county, slander could still be tried as libel.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个郡，口头中伤仍然可以按诽谤起诉。
senses.why: Legal systems pooled written and spoken defamation under one name, stretching the written sense wider.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系把书面与口头的毁誉归到同一个名称下，使原本的书面义变宽。

intro.en: Libel goes back to Latin libellus, a little book, a small written statement, through Old French libelle.
intro.cn: libel 源自拉丁语 libellus（小书、短文），经古法语 libelle 进入英语。

items.en: Liber is a book and libellus is its small form.
items.cn: liber 意为书，libellus 是它的指小形式。

items.en: Libellus serves as a written petition or claim in law.
items.cn: libellus 在法律中指书面的诉状或主张。

items.en: Libelle names a little book or a written accusation.
items.cn: libelle 指小册子或书面的指控。

items.en: The word first means a formal written statement filed in court.
items.cn: 该词初入英语时指在法庭提交的正式文书。

items.en: Libel comes to mean a defamatory publication.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，libel 转指毁人名誉的出版物。

items.en: Legal English sharpens libel into written or printed defamation.
items.cn: 现代法律英语把 libel 固定为书面或印刷形式的诽谤。

note.en: Libel shares the little book root with library and pamphlet, and stands beside slander and defamation.
note.cn: libel 与 library、pamphlet 共享「小书」这一词根，并在意义上与 slander、defamation 相邻。

entries.definition: a place where books are kept for use
entries.definitionCN: 图书馆（与 libellus 同源的「书」）

entries.definition: containing a false statement that damages a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 诽谤性的；含毁誉内容的

entries.definition: the text of an opera or a musical work
entries.definitionCN: 歌剧剧本（与「小书」同源）

entries.definition: false spoken words that damage a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 口头诽谤（对应书面的 libel）

entries.definition: the act of harming a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 毁誉；诽谤（统称）

entries.definition: a deliberate attack on someones good name
entries.definitionCN: 抹黑；中伤

normalIntro.en: Libel is a little book of lies: libellus carries damage inside its printing.
normalIntro.cn: libel 是一本写着谎言的小书：libellus 把伤害印在纸里。

normal.en: Sue for libel is the step a damaged person takes.
normal.cn: sue for libel 是受害者采取的一步。

normal.en: Compare slander: spoken hurt is slander, printed hurt is libel.
normal.cn: 对比 slander：说出口的伤害是 slander，印在纸上的伤害是 libel。

normal.en: The family link with library keeps the book inside the word.
normal.cn: 与 library 的同源关系提醒你：这个词里藏着一本书。

normal.en: Libellous is the adjective that describes a libellous claim.
normal.cn: libellous 就是用来形容诽谤性说法的形容词。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l in libelled, American spelling keeps one.
normal.cn: 英式拼写把 l 双写成 libelled，美式拼写则只写一个。

abstract.en: See a printed page with black ink dripping onto a persons name.
abstract.cn: 想象一页印刷品，黑墨一滴滴落在某个人的名字上。

abstract.en: Picture a small book passed around a crowd, each reader nodding.
abstract.cn: 想象一本小书在人群里传阅，每人都点头。

abstract.en: Imagine a rumour typed out and pinned to a notice board.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言被打成字，钉在公告栏上。

examples.en: The actor brought a libel action against the tabloid.
examples.cn: 那位演员对小报提起了诽谤诉讼。

examples.en: Publishing those claims could leave the paper open to libel.
examples.cn: 刊出那些说法会让报纸面临诽谤诉讼的风险。

examples.en: The journalist knew the libels in the leaflet were illegal.
examples.cn: 那名记者知道传单里的诽谤文字是违法的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来不」——有人在背后说「来不」及的事，就是文字诽谤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 liber（书）→ 指小形式 libellus（小书、书面诉状）→ 古法语 libelle → 英语 libel，词源本义「小册子」，后来转指以文字毁人名誉。

sensesIntro.en: Libel moves from a written claim in court to a written injury, then to the offending text and to the act itself.
sensesIntro.cn: libel 从法庭上的书面诉状，转为以文字造成的伤害，再指那篇惹祸的文字以及施加伤害的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed leaflet that throws ink at a person name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张往人名上泼墨的印刷传单。

branches.en: The legal wrong of written damage is the main sense.
branches.cn: 书面毁誉的法律过错是主义项。

branches.en: The offending text is the concrete noun sense.
branches.cn: 惹祸的文字是具体的名词义项。

branches.en: The verb sense is the act of causing such damage.
branches.cn: 动词义项即施加这类伤害的动作。

branches.en: Church petitions and wide legal uses keep the older written claim alive.
branches.cn: 教会诉状与较宽的法律用法保留了更早的书面主张义。

branches.en: The wrong and the text that caused it are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 过错与造成过错的文字用同一个词指称。

intro.en: Libel grows from the Latin book word liber, with library, libretto, and libellous in the same family.
intro.cn: libel 由拉丁语表示「书」的 liber 生长而来，library、libretto、libellous 同属这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber is a book and the bark used for writing, and libellus is its small form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 liber 指书与书写用的树皮，libellus 是它的指小形式。

items.meaning: book, the inner bark of a tree
items.example: Liber supplies the book image.
items.exampleCN: liber 提供「书」的意象。

items.example: The suffix makes libellus a little book.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾使 libellus 成为「小书」。

items.meaning: a little book, a written claim
items.example: Libellus is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: libellus 是直接源头。

items.example: Old French carries it into law.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把它带入法律语境。

items.example: Libel keeps the written sense.
items.exampleCN: libel 保留了书面这一层。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix forms libellous.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 libellous。

items.meaning: a collection or building of books
items.example: Library shares the book root.
items.exampleCN: library 共享「书」这一词根。

items.meaning: a small book of opera text
items.example: Libretto repeats the little book form.
items.exampleCN: libretto 重现了「小书」这一形式。

items.meaning: a plaintiff in a libel case
items.example: The -ant suffix names the suing party.
items.exampleCN: -ant 词尾指提起诉讼的一方。

definition_zh: 死的；无生命的；死气沉沉的；呆板的；失去活力的
definition_en: no longer alive, or lacking energy and liveliness
core_image: 一截断了的树枝躺在雪地上，没有一点动静
scene: 沙漠里风一直吹，地平线看上去单调又毫无生气。The desert stretched out under the sun, lifeless and flat for miles around.
sceneCN: 这里 lifeless 是「死气沉沉的」（第 2 个义项：没有生命气息、缺乏活力）；句意：沙漠在烈日下铺展开去，方圆数里死气沉沉，平坦无物。

pos.zh: 死的；无生命的
死气沉沉的；乏味的
呆板的；无生气的

derivatives.zh: lifeless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「毫无生气地」
lifeless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「死寂；无生气」
以 life 加 like 构成的同族词，义为「栩栩如生的」，与词尾 less 相对

senses.title: No longer alive
senses.definition: dead, or showing no sign of life
senses.definitionCN: 已经死亡的，或毫无生命迹象的
senses.example: The bird lay lifeless on the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟一动不动地躺在草地上，已经死了。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, so lifeless is the plain picture of a body with no life left in it.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -less 意为「没有」，所以 lifeless 就是一具里外都没有了生命的躯体的直白画面。

senses.title: Dull and without energy
senses.definition: dull, flat, or lacking energy, as of a place, activity, or style
senses.definitionCN: 指地方、活动或风格沉闷、平淡、缺乏活力
senses.example: The town felt lifeless after the festival ended.
senses.exampleCN: 节日过后，这座小镇显得死气沉沉。
senses.why: When the life is not bodily but social, without life slides easily into without any spark.
senses.whyCN: 当这里的「生命」不是身体而是社会气息时，「没有生命」顺理成章地滑向「没有一点火花」。

senses.title: Wooden and mechanical
senses.definition: stiff and without natural expression or feeling, as of a face, voice, or manner
senses.definitionCN: 指面部、声音或举止僵硬、不自然、没有情感
senses.example: He read the speech in a lifeless voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他用毫无生气的声音念完讲稿。
senses.why: A person who speaks and moves without life feels like a machine, so the word describes wooden delivery too.
senses.whyCN: 一个说话与动作都「没有生命」的人像机器，于是这个词也用来形容刻板的表达。

senses.title: Having no living things
senses.definition: describing a setting or world in which nothing lives or grows
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个环境中没有任何生命存在或生长
senses.example: Seen from space, the moon is a lifeless rock.
senses.exampleCN: 从太空看，月球是一块没有生命的岩石。
senses.why: Without life applied to a whole place turns the adjective into a description of a habitat or a world.
senses.whyCN: 把「没有生命」用于一整个环境时，这个形容词就变成对栖息地或星球的描述。

intro.en: Lifeless is an English compound of life and the suffix -less, without, built on an unreconstructable Old English noun.
intro.cn: lifeless 是英语自造的复合词，由 life 加后缀 -less（没有）构成，其中 life 的古英语源头来源不确定。

items.en: The noun behind life is thought to mean a continuing existence.
items.cn: life 背后的日耳曼语名词一般认为表示持续的存在。

items.en: Lif names life or a living body.
items.cn: 古英语 lif 指生命或活着的身体。

items.en: The suffix -laus means lacking something.
items.cn: 后缀 -laus 意为缺少某物，是 -less 的前身。

items.en: The compound grows into a settled adjective for what has no life.
items.cn: 该复合词在中古英语中固定下来，指没有生命的事物。

items.en: The adjective widens to describe dull places, voices, and writing.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个形容词扩展到沉闷的场所、声音与文笔。

note.en: Lifeless pairs life with the suffix -less, and sits near dead, lifelike, and spiritless.
note.cn: lifeless 把 life 与后缀 -less 组合在一起，意义上靠近 dead、lifelike 与 spiritless。

entries.definition: having no limits at all
entries.definitionCN: 无限的（与 lifeless 共用 -less）

entries.definition: looking or sounding like a real person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 栩栩如生的（同用 life 词干，词尾相反）

entries.definition: a small boat used to rescue people at sea
entries.definitionCN: 救生艇（与 life 构成的复合词）

entries.definition: no longer living
entries.definitionCN: 死的；无生命的

entries.definition: not interesting or not bright
entries.definitionCN: 沉闷的；昏暗的

entries.definition: without power to move or act
entries.definitionCN: 不活动的；惰性的

normalIntro.en: Lifeless is life minus life: the suffix -less simply takes it away.
normalIntro.cn: lifeless 就是 life 减去生命本身：词尾 -less 直接把它拿走。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without, so lifeless is without life from the start.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 意为「没有」，所以 lifeless 从头就是「没有生命」。

normal.en: A lifeless body is a body with nothing moving inside.
normal.cn: lifeless body 是里面再无任何动静的身体。

normal.en: A lifeless voice is flat and mechanical, with no feeling.
normal.cn: lifeless voice 是平板机械、没有感情的声音。

normal.en: Set lifelike against lifeless: like means it seems alive, less means it does not.
normal.cn: 把 lifelike 与 lifeless 对照：like 是「看起来像活着」，less 是「不再活着」。

normal.en: Compare dead and dull: lifeless works for both bodies and moods.
normal.cn: 对比 dead 与 dull：lifeless 既能形容身体，也能形容气氛。

abstract.en: Picture a branch snapped off a tree and lying in the snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一截从树上折下、躺在雪里的树枝。

abstract.en: See a stage set with the lights off and nobody on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个灯已熄灭、空无一人的舞台布景。

abstract.en: Imagine a robot repeating its greeting for the third time.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器人第三次重复同一句问候。

examples.en: The fish floated lifeless in the shallow water.
examples.cn: 那条鱼在浅水里漂着，已经没有生命迹象。

examples.en: After the factory closed, the village became lifeless.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，村子变得毫无生气。

examples.en: His lifeless reply told us he had lost interest.
examples.cn: 他呆板地回答，说明已经没了兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福 lost」——原本的「来福」都丢了，自然一片死气沉沉；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lif（生命）配日耳曼语词尾 -laus（缺少）→ 中古英语 lifles → 现代英语 lifeless，核心义「没有生命」。

sensesIntro.en: Lifeless begins with a body without life, then spreads to places without energy and to faces or voices without feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: lifeless 从「身体没有生命」出发，再扩展到「场所没有活力」，以及「面容或声音没有感情」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken branch lying still in the snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一截断枝静静躺在雪地上。

branches.en: Not being alive is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 没有生命是字面义项。

branches.en: A place without energy is the extended sense.
branches.cn: 缺乏活力的场所是引申义项。

branches.en: A wooden face or voice is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 呆板的面容或声音是比喻义项。

branches.en: A world without living things is the widest sense.
branches.cn: 没有任何生物的世界是最宽的义项。

branches.en: Both a dull place and a stiff voice feel as if the spark has gone.
branches.cn: 沉闷的场所与僵硬的声音都让人觉得那点火花已经熄灭。

intro.en: Lifeless is life plus the privative suffix -less, with lifelike, lifelessly, and lifelessness built around it.
intro.cn: lifeless 由 life 加表「缺乏」的后缀 -less 构成，lifelike、lifelessly 与 lifelessness 围绕它扩展。

latinIntro.en: The core word life has no secure Latin ancestor, so Latin matches are few.
latinIntro.cn: 核心词 life 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先，因此可列的拉丁同源词很少。

items.example: Life is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: life 是该复合词的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns life into lifeless.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把 life 变成 lifeless。

items.example: The suffix forms lifelessly.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 lifelessly。

items.example: The suffix forms lifelessness.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 lifelessness。

items.example: The suffix forms lifelike.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 lifelike。

items.meaning: in a dull or mechanical way
items.example: Lifelessly keeps the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: lifelessly 保留了形容词词干。

items.meaning: the quality of having no life
items.example: Lifelessness names the state.
items.exampleCN: lifelessness 指这种状态。

items.example: Lifelike is the opposite partner.
items.exampleCN: lifelike 是意义相反的伙伴词。

items.meaning: a rope or route on which survival depends
items.example: Lifeline joins life with line.
items.exampleCN: lifeline 由 life 与 line 合成。

definition_zh: 救生员；救命的人或物；救命稻草
definition_en: a person or thing that saves someone from danger, or something that gives help at a crucial moment
core_image: 溺水中被一只手抓住，把人拖回岸边
scene: 暴雨后的海滩浪很急，一个少年被回浪卷走，救生员冲进水里把他拉回沙滩。After the storm, the waves grew fierce, and the lifesaver pulled the boy out of the current.
sceneCN: 这里 lifesaver 是「救生员」（第 1 个义项：在海滩或泳池救人的人）；句意：暴雨后海浪很大，救生员把少年从激流中拉了出来。

pos.zh: 救生员；救命的人或物；救急之物

life 与 save 加 -ing 构成，义为「救生的」

senses.title: A person who rescues swimmers
senses.definition: a person who is trained to rescue people from water, especially at a beach or pool
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、能在海滩或泳池中救人的人
senses.example: The lifesaver blew the whistle to warn the swimmers.
senses.exampleCN: 救生员吹哨警告游泳的人。
senses.why: The two halves give life plus a rescuer, so the first sense is literally a person who keeps life safe.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「生命」加「拯救者」拼成，所以第一个义项就是字面上把人命救回来的人。

senses.title: Anything that rescues someone
senses.definition: an object or device that saves a person from drowning or serious harm
senses.definitionCN: 能把人从溺水或严重伤害中救出的物件或装置
senses.example: A life jacket can be a real lifesaver in rough seas.
senses.exampleCN: 在波涛汹涌的海面上，救生衣真的是救命之物。
senses.why: From a rescuing person the word widens to rescuing things, such as vests, belts, and lifeboats.
senses.whyCN: 从「救人的人」扩展到「救人的东西」，救生衣、救生圈和救生艇都算，这是词义由人到物的自然延伸。

senses.title: Something that helps in a crisis
senses.definition: something that prevents a serious problem at exactly the moment it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 恰在需要时防止严重问题的东西或办法
senses.example: Your spare umbrella was a lifesaver this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早你的备用雨伞真是救了我。
senses.why: Everyday use softens the rescue image: a handy item that appears at the right moment feels like a rescue.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把「救人」的画面弱化了：在关键时刻恰好出现的实用之物，感觉就像被救了一把。

senses.title: A person who gives vital help
senses.definition: a person whose help is essential and timely
senses.definitionCN: 提供关键而及时帮助的人
senses.example: My neighbour was a lifesaver when my car broke down.
senses.exampleCN: 我的车抛锚时，邻居真是帮了大忙。
senses.why: Spoken English returns the word to people, this time for ordinary timely help rather than a rescue from water.
senses.whyCN: 口语又把这个词还给「人」，只是这里指日常中的及时援手，而不是从水里救人。

senses.title: A rescue swimmer or guard in sport
senses.definition: in surf life saving competitions, an athlete who uses rescue skills and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 在冲浪救生比赛中使用救生技能和装备的选手
senses.example: She trains as a lifesaver every summer weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天的周末她都在做救生员训练。
senses.why: The lifeguard sense turned into a sport, so a lifesaver can now also name a competitor.
senses.whyCN: 救生员这一含义发展成了运动项目，所以 lifesaver 也用来指参赛的救生选手。

intro.en: Lifesaver is a modern English compound of life and a rescuer derived from the verb save.
intro.cn: lifesaver 是现代英语的合成词，由 life（生命）和 save（救）派生的「拯救者」组合而成。

items.en: Lif and sarian are the early English words for life and rescue.
items.cn: 古英语用 lif 表示生命，用 sarian 表示救。

items.en: Save comes in from Old French sauver, with the same Latin salvus, safe, behind it.
items.cn: save 经古法语 sauver 进入英语，背后同为拉丁语 salvus（安全）。

items.en: Trade catalogues begin to advertise saving life as a product in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪的商品目录开始把「救生」作为产品卖点。

items.en: Lifesaver appears as a compound for a rescuer and later for rescue equipment.
items.cn: lifesaver 作为合成词出现，最初指救人者，后来也指救生设备。

items.en: Informal use extends the word to anything that helps at a critical moment.
items.cn: 非正式用法把它扩展到在关键时刻起作用的任何东西。

note.en: Lifesaver sits between lifesaving skills, lifeguard jobs, and everyday words for help.
note.cn: lifesaver 处在「救生技能」「救生员职业」与日常「帮助」词汇之间。

normalIntro.en: Life plus saver shows the whole idea in three parts of a word: someone or something that keeps life safe.
normalIntro.cn: life 加 saver 把整层意思写在词里：保住生命的人或物。

normal.en: The words life and saver are joined, so a lifesaver is literally one who saves life.
normal.cn: life 与 saver 直接相连，所以 lifesaver 字面就是「救人性命者」。

normal.en: You can be a lifesaver with a kind act: giving cash to a friend who has lost a wallet.
normal.cn: 一句贴心之举也能当 lifesaver：把钱借给丢了钱包的朋友。

normal.en: A lifesaver must be quick, so the phrase be a lifesaver signals urgent help.
normal.cn: 救生之人必须快，所以 be a lifesaver 就是「及时救命；帮了大忙」。

normal.en: A life jacket is a lifesaver, so safety items often carry the word life.
normal.cn: 救生衣是 lifesaver，许多安全用品都带着 life 这个词。

normal.en: In British English a lifeguard works at pools, while a lifesaver often trains in rescue clubs.
normal.cn: 英式英语里 lifeguard 在泳池值班，lifesaver 更多指参加救生训练的救生员。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a rope thrown from the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手紧紧抓住从岸边抛来的绳子。

abstract.en: See a red life jacket floating where the sea is rough.
abstract.cn: 想象一件红色救生衣在波涛里浮着。

abstract.en: Think of a cheap umbrella that suddenly opened in a downpour.
abstract.cn: 想象一把廉价的雨伞在暴雨里突然撑开。

examples.en: The lifesaver reached the swimmer before the current took him.
examples.cn: 救生员在激流把人卷走之前够到了那名游泳者。

examples.en: The small fan was a lifesaver during the hottest week of summer.
examples.cn: 在夏天最热的那一周，那台小风扇真是救命之物。

examples.en: Just a phone call from you would be a lifesaver for me.
examples.cn: 你打来一个电话，对我就真是帮了大忙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福sei啊」——来了福气、把人从水里救上岸，救命的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lif（生命）+ 古法语 sauver（救，源自拉丁语 salvus「安全」）→ lifesaver，核心义「把性命挽救回来的人或物」。

sensesIntro.en: Lifesaver starts as a person who rescues swimmers, widens to rescue equipment, then to anything or anyone that appears at a critical moment.
sensesIntro.cn: lifesaver 先指在水里救人的救生员，再扩展到救生设备，最后泛指在关键时刻出现的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand grabbing a rescuer and being pulled back to land.
core.cn: 核心意象：溺水者抓住救援的手，被拖回岸上。

branches.en: The rescuer in water is the first and most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 水中的救人者是第一个也最具体的义项。

branches.en: Equipment that saves lives extends the rescuer image to objects.
branches.cn: 救生设备把「救人者」的形象延伸到物件上。

branches.en: Everyday help in a crisis is the softened figurative sense.
branches.cn: 危机中的日常帮助是这个义项的弱化比喻用法。

branches.en: Both senses name a person who saves, one professionally and one informally.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都指救人者，一个是职业身份，一个是日常说法。

branches.en: The guard sense grew into a rescue sport with its own competitors.
branches.cn: 救生员含义发展成救生运动，有了自己的参赛选手。

intro.en: Lifesaver joins two native and French elements: life from Old English and save from Latin salvus by way of French.
intro.cn: lifesaver 把两个来源不同的词素拼在一起：life 出自古英语，save 经法语来自拉丁语 salvus。

latinIntro.en: Latin salvus means safe, and it lies behind salvare, save, and salvator, saviour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salvus 意为「安全的」，它衍生出 salvare（救）和 salvator（救主）。

definition_zh: 一生；终生；使用寿命；漫长的一段时间
definition_en: the length of time that a person or thing exists or continues to work
core_image: 一条从出生延伸到终点的长线
scene: 老木匠抚摸着用了半辈子的刨子，说这工具陪了他一生。The old carpenter held the plane he had used for decades and said it had been with him a lifetime.
sceneCN: 这里 lifetime 是「一生；终生」（第 1 个义项：人活着的那段时间）；句意：老木匠说这把用了半辈子的刨子陪了他一生。

pos.zh: 一生；终生；使用寿命；漫长时段
终身的；一辈子的

derivatives.zh: life 与 long 复合，义为「终身的；一辈子的」，与 lifetime 意思相近但用法不同
life 与 span（跨度）复合，义为「寿命；有效期」
time 加 -ly 构成，义为「及时的」，共享时间词根
time 加 -less 构成，义为「永恒的；不受时间影响的」

senses.title: The length of a person life
senses.definition: the period of time during which a person is alive
senses.definitionCN: 一个人活着的整段时间
senses.example: He spent a lifetime working on the same farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他一辈子都在同一座农场上干活。
senses.why: Life plus time simply stretches life across its full length, so the word first means the whole span of a person being alive.
senses.whyCN: life 加 time 就是把「生命」铺展成一条完整的时间线，所以第一义就是一个人从生到死的全程。

senses.title: The whole time something lasts
senses.definition: the entire period for which an animal, plant, or object exists
senses.definitionCN: 动物、植物或物体存在的整段时间
senses.example: A tortoise may live for a lifetime of two hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 一只陆龟的一生可能长达两百年。
senses.why: If life can be borrowed for non-human beings, then a machine or an animal also has a lifetime.
senses.whyCN: 既然「life」可以借给非人的生物，机器或动物自然也有一条属于自己的时间线。

senses.title: How long an item works
senses.definition: the period during which a product, battery, or machine can be used
senses.definitionCN: 产品、电池或机器可以使用的时段
senses.example: The battery has a lifetime of about five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这种电池的使用寿命大约五年。
senses.why: Technical English asks how long a thing lives, so lifetime becomes a measurable service life.
senses.whyCN: 技术英语要问一件东西「能活多久」，于是 lifetime 变成可测量的使用寿命。

senses.title: A very long stretch of time
senses.definition: an informally long period, longer than seems reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 口语中显得异常漫长的一段时间
senses.example: I waited a lifetime for the bus this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早我等公交等到仿佛过了一辈子。
senses.why: Hyperbole treats a boring wait as if it were a whole life, giving the loose sense of a very long time.
senses.whyCN: 夸张说法把无聊的等待比作整整一辈子，于是有了「漫长一段时间」的松散义。

senses.title: Lasting for a whole life
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean lasting for all of a person life
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示持续一生的
senses.example: She won a lifetime membership to the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她获得了俱乐部的终身会员资格。
senses.why: The noun moved in front of another noun and turned into an adjective, as in lifetime achievement.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词跑到另一个名词前面，就变成形容词，例如 lifetime achievement。

intro.en: Lifetime is a native English compound of life and time, though time itself came in from Old English tima by way of Norse influence.
intro.cn: lifetime 是本土英语合成词，由 life 与 time 组成；time 本身承自古英语 tima，并受古诺斯语影响。

items.en: Lif and tima are the early words for life and a span of time.
items.cn: 古英语用 lif 表示生命，用 tima 表示一段时间。

items.en: Old Norse timi strengthens the form time in the north and middle of England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 timi 加强了英格兰北部和中部 time 这一形式。

items.en: Lifetimes first names the span of a single person living, often in legal and poetic text.
items.cn: lifetimes 最早指一个人活着的时间跨度，常见于法律与诗歌文本。

items.en: The word widens to animals, plants, and lasting things beyond people.
items.cn: 词义扩展到动物、植物以及人以外能长久存在的东西。

items.en: Industry and advertising add the sense of service life for products and batteries.
items.cn: 工业与广告让它多出「产品、电池的使用寿命」这一义。

note.en: Lifetime is a time-span compound, close to lifespan and lifelong, and to words for the extent of life.
note.cn: lifetime 是表示时间跨度的合成词，与 lifespan、lifelong 接近，也与「一生时长」类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Life plus time draws one straight line: how much time a life or a thing gets.
normalIntro.cn: life 加 time 画出一条直线：一条生命或一件东西能得到多少时间。

normal.en: The words are simply life and time, so a lifetime is the time of a life.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 life 与 time 相加，所以 lifetime 就是「一生的时间」。

normal.en: Once in a lifetime means only one such chance will ever come.
normal.cn: once in a lifetime 意味着这样的机会一生只有一次。

normal.en: A lifetime achievement award honours a whole career.
normal.cn: lifetime achievement 奖是表彰整个职业生涯的奖项。

normal.en: For machines, a lifetime is measured in years of service, not feelings.
normal.cn: 对机器而言，lifetime 按使用年限算，而不是按感受算。

normal.en: Compare lifelong: lifelong is an adjective for continuous things, lifetime can also be a noun.
normal.cn: 对比 lifelong：lifelong 是表示持续状态的形容词，lifetime 也可以作名词。

abstract.en: Picture a long rope stretched from a baby blanket to an old cane.
abstract.cn: 想象一根长绳，从婴儿毯一直拉到老人的拐杖。

abstract.en: See a battery gauge slowly draining from full to empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一块电池的指示灯从满格一点点变空。

abstract.en: Imagine waiting at a bus stop while the sun rises and sets.
abstract.cn: 想象在公交站等车，看着太阳升起又落下。

examples.en: She has collected stamps for a lifetime.
examples.cn: 她收集邮票已经收集了一辈子。

examples.en: Tickets to that concert were the chance of a lifetime.
examples.cn: 那场音乐会的门票是千载难逢的机会。

examples.en: Lifetimes of research went into this single vaccine.
examples.cn: 这一支疫苗背后是几代人一生的研究。

sensesIntro.en: Lifetime begins as the whole span of a human life, extends to animals and objects, narrows to a product service life, and loosens into a very long time or an adjective for lasting things.
sensesIntro.cn: lifetime 先指人的整个人生，扩展到动物与器物，再专指产品的使用寿命，最后松散化为「漫长一段时间」或表示「终身的」形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long line from birth to the final point.
core.cn: 核心意象：从出生到终点的一条长线。

branches.en: The whole life of a person is the base sense.
branches.cn: 一个人的整个人生是基础义项。

branches.en: The same span applied to animals and objects extends the line beyond people.
branches.cn: 把同一条时间线套到动物与器物上，就超出了人的范围。

branches.en: Product lifetime is the measured technical version of the span.
branches.cn: 产品寿命是这条时间线的技术化度量版本。

branches.en: Exaggerated waiting turns the whole span into a long and tedious stretch.
branches.cn: 夸张的等待把整条时间线变成漫长难熬的一段。

branches.en: The noun standing before another noun turns into a lifetime adjective.
branches.cn: 名词放在另一名词前，就变成表示「终身的」形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies many time words, such as tempus for time and vita for life, though neither is the direct source of lifetime.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语能提供许多时间词，如 tempus（时间）和 vita（生命），但它们都不是 lifetime 的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: lightweight 的前半部分，义为「轻的」
lightweight 的后半部分，义为「重量」
weight 加 -y 构成，义为「沉重的；有分量的」，与 lightweight 的比喻义相对
light 加 -ness 构成，义为「轻；轻盈」

senses.title: Weighing less than usual
senses.definition: weighing less than other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类东西重量更小
senses.example: The store sells lightweight backpacks for hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售给徒步者用的轻量背包。
senses.why: Light means not heavy and weight means mass, so the compound just states a small weight.
senses.whyCN: light 是「轻的」，weight 是「重量」，组合起来就是字面上的「重量小」。

senses.title: Easy to carry or wear
senses.definition: thin, compact, or easy to carry, especially of clothing and tools
senses.definitionCN: 薄、便携、易于携带，尤指衣物和工具
senses.example: Take a lightweight jacket in case the evening turns cool.
senses.exampleCN: 带一件轻便外套，以防晚上变凉。
senses.why: For things you carry, a small weight also means easy handling, so lightweight comes to mean portable.
senses.whyCN: 对随身携带的东西来说，重量小也意味着好拿，于是 lightweight 引申为「便携、轻便」。

senses.title: Not serious or important
senses.titleCN: 无关紧要的；乏善可陈的
senses.definition: lacking depth or weight, often used to criticise something weak
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏深度或分量，常用于批评东西薄弱
senses.example: The report was pleasant but lightweight.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告读着舒服，却没什么分量。
senses.why: Figurative English treats weight as seriousness, so something light in weight becomes light in value.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法把「重量」等同于「分量」，于是物理上的轻就变成价值上的单薄。

senses.title: Belonging to a light weight class
senses.definition: of the class of competitors below middleweight in boxing, rowing, and similar sports
senses.definitionCN: 拳击、赛艇等运动中低于中量级的级别
senses.example: She fought as a lightweight boxer for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 她当了十年轻量级拳击手。
senses.why: Sports weigh athletes into classes, and the light class gives the noun and adjective lightweight.
senses.whyCN: 体育按体重分级，较轻的那一级给出 lightweight 这个名词和形容词。

senses.title: A person of little influence
senses.definition: an informal term for a person who lacks ability or importance
senses.definitionCN: 口语中称缺乏能力或分量的人
senses.example: He is regarded as a lightweight by his rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 在对手眼里，他是个无足轻重的人。
senses.why: The boxing class turns into a label for influence, so a lightweight is someone who does not weigh enough to matter.
senses.whyCN: 拳击级别变成评价影响力大小的标签：轻量级的人，分量不够，不被重视。

intro.en: Lightweight joins two native words: light from Old English leoht, not heavy, and weight from Old English gewiht.
intro.cn: lightweight 由两个本土词合成：light 出自古英语 leoht（轻的），weight 出自古英语 gewiht（重量）。

items.en: Leoht means not heavy, and gewiht means the heaviness of a thing.
items.cn: leoht 表示「不重的」，gewiht 表示「物体的重量」。

items.en: The two words settle as light and weight and are often paired in trade talk.
items.cn: 两者逐渐定型为 light 与 weight，常在交易用语中并列使用。

items.en: Trade and horse racing describe light weight loads and small weights.
items.cn: 十八世纪的贸易与赛马中已经用 light weight 描述轻的载重与轻微量级。

items.en: Prize fighting adopts lightweight as the name of a weight class.
items.cn: 十九世纪拳击运动采用 lightweight 作为一个体重级别的名称。

items.en: The word spreads from sport to products and then to people of little substance.
items.cn: 这个词从体育扩展到产品，再用来形容分量不足的人。

note.en: Lightweight is a compound of light and weight, close to other weight words and to terms for light or unimportant things.
note.cn: lightweight 是 light 与 weight 的合成词，与其它重量词以及「轻、不重要」类词相邻。

entries.definition: heavy or serious
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；重要的

entries.definition: how heavy something is
entries.definitionCN: 重量；分量

entries.definition: a very light boxing class
entries.definitionCN: 羽量级；极轻的类别

entries.definition: a boxing class above lightweight
entries.definitionCN: 中量级（高于轻量级）

entries.definition: light and easy to carry
entries.definitionCN: 便携的

entries.definition: thin and weak, not solid
entries.definitionCN: 脆弱的；不结实的

entries.definition: of little importance
entries.definitionCN: 琐碎的；不重要的

normalIntro.en: Light plus weight says the whole thing: the compound names a small amount of heaviness.
normalIntro.cn: light 加 weight 已经把意思说清：这个词指很小的一份重量。

normal.en: Light means not heavy and weight means mass, so lightweight is simply low weight.
normal.cn: light 是不重，weight 是质量，所以 lightweight 就是「重量小」。

normal.en: A lightweight jacket is thin and easy to pack, so lightweight product words are practical.
normal.cn: lightweight jacket 薄而易打包，所以这个词常用来描述实用产品。

normal.en: In sports the word names a weight class, like featherweight and middleweight.
normal.cn: 在体育中它指一个体重级别，与 featherweight、middleweight 同类。

normal.en: Calling a plan lightweight means it lacks weight, that is, depth.
normal.cn: 说一个计划 lightweight，意思是它没分量、缺深度。

normal.en: Compare weighty: weighty is heavy or serious, the opposite of lightweight.
normal.cn: 对比 weighty：它表示沉重或重要，是 lightweight 的反面。

abstract.en: Picture a feather-filled backpack lifted with two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象用两根手指就提起一只装满羽毛的背包。

abstract.en: See a thin jacket folded into a pocket like a sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一件薄外套像纸一样折进口袋。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that barely moves when a small box is placed on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小盒子放上秤，指针几乎不动。

examples.en: Cyclists pay a lot for lightweight frames made of carbon.
examples.cn: 骑行者为碳纤维制成的轻质车架花了不少钱。

examples.en: The film got good reviews but was considered lightweight by critics.
examples.cn: 这部电影获得了好评，却被评论家认为分量不足。

examples.en: In the lightweight final, the younger boxer moved much faster.
examples.cn: 在轻量级决赛中，较年轻的拳手动作明显更快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖特威特」——赖特体重很轻特轻，轻得像羽毛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 leoht（轻的，不重）+ gewiht（重量）→ lightweight，核心义「重量小；分量轻」。

sensesIntro.en: Lightweight starts as a physical description of low weight, becomes ease of carrying, turns into a judgement of little importance, and finally names a sports class and a person of little influence.
sensesIntro.cn: lightweight 先描述物理上的重量小，再指便于携带，随后转为「不重要」的评价，最后指体育中的体重级别和影响力小的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a backpack that lifts with two fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：两指就能提起的背包。

branches.en: Low physical weight is the literal and central sense.
branches.cn: 物理重量小是字面与核心义项。

branches.en: For carried things, low weight becomes convenience.
branches.cn: 对被携带的物品来说，轻就等于方便。

branches.en: Weight as seriousness gives the critical figurative sense.
branches.cn: 把重量看作严肃性，就得到批判性的比喻义。

branches.en: Sporting classes take their names from the measured weight.
branches.cn: 体育级别直接以实际重量命名。

branches.en: The sports class becomes a label for a person without influence.
branches.cn: 体育级别又变成对影响力不足之人的标签。

intro.en: Lightweight is a transparent compound of light and weight, and it sits inside the wider weight family of featherweight and middleweight.
intro.cn: lightweight 是 light 与 weight 的透明合成词，并且属于 featherweight、middleweight 这一更大的重量类词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin levis means light in weight, and its relatives also gave English levity and levitate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levis 意为「轻的」，其同族词还给英语带来 levity 和 levitate。

items.example: Light is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: light 是合成词的前半部分。

items.example: Weight is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: weight 是合成词的后半部分。

items.example: The suffix -y forms weighty from weight.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 weight 变成 weighty。

items.example: Weighty is the opposite of lightweight.
items.exampleCN: weighty 是 lightweight 的反义词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms lightness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 lightness。

items.meaning: the quality of not being heavy
items.example: Lightness names the quality behind lightweight.
items.exampleCN: lightness 指出 lightweight 背后的性质。

items.example: Featherweight and middleweight use the same -weight ending.
items.exampleCN: featherweight 和 middleweight 使用同样的后部。

items.example: Featherweight sits below lightweight.
items.exampleCN: 羽量级低于轻量级。

items.example: Middleweight sits above lightweight.
items.exampleCN: 中量级高于轻量级。

definition_zh: 可能性；概率；希望
definition_en: the chance that something will happen or be true
core_image: 天平的一端压着厚厚的云层，另一端悬在空中
scene: 天气节目的主持人把云图推到镜头前，又指着日历上标红的那一天说雨快来了。The likelihood of heavy rain on the coast is higher than in the hills this week.
sceneCN: 这里 likelihood 是「可能性」（第 1 个义项：某事发生的几率）；句意为本周沿海出现大雨的可能性高于山区。画面中的主要对象：云图、日历上标红的一天、镜头前的天气主持人。

pos.zh: 可能性；概率；希望

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -hood 得到的基础形容词，义为「很可能的；大概」
由 likely 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「可能性」，与本词同义但较少使用
由否定前缀 un- 加 likely 构成，义为「不太可能的」

senses.title: The chance that something will happen
senses.definition: the chance that an event will take place or that a statement is true
senses.definitionCN: 某件事将会发生，或某种说法属实的几率
senses.example: The likelihood of a strike this autumn has risen sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 今年秋天罢工的可能性大幅上升。
senses.why: The word is built on likely, which meant having the appearance of something, so likelihood is the measure of how much an event looks set to happen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 likely 加后缀构成，likely 原指「看样子像某物」，因此 likelihood 就是衡量一件事「看起来有多少把握会发生」的尺度。

senses.title: A statistical probability
senses.definition: in statistics, the probability assigned to an outcome under a stated model
senses.definitionCN: 在统计学中，在既定模型下给某个结果赋予的概率
senses.example: The model gives a likelihood of ninety per cent for the warmer scenario.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型认为偏暖情景的概率为九成。
senses.why: Once the everyday guess is measured in numbers, it becomes the formal likelihood of statistics and forecasting.
senses.whyCN: 当日常的猜测被换算成数字，它就变成统计学与预测中正式的「概率」义。

senses.title: A promising state or prospect
senses.definition: the quality of something promising success or of a favourable outlook
senses.definitionCN: 某事物有成功希望或前景良好的性质
senses.example: That approach offers real likelihood of solving the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 那种方法确实有解决这个问题的希望。
senses.why: The old sense of looking right for a part survived in likelihood as the promise a plan or method holds out.
senses.whyCN: 「看着正合适」这一旧义留在 likelihood 里，指的是某个方案或方法所展现出的希望。

intro.en: Likelihood joins likely with the abstract noun ending -hood; the base likely grew from like, which meant having the same appearance as something.
intro.cn: likelihood 由 likely 加抽象名词后缀 -hood 构成；基础词 likely 源自 like，原义是「看起来和某物相像」。

items.en: A root reconstructed as lika- is generally taken to mean body or form, and from it came words for being alike in shape.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 lika-，意为「身体、形状」，由此产生表示「外形相似」的词。

items.en: Old English -lic was an abstract ending meaning form or state, and gelic meant alike; the modern -hood comes from Old English -had, meaning condition.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -lic 表示「形状、样态」，gelic 意为「相像」；现代后缀 -hood 来自古英语 -had，意为「状态」。

items.en: Middle English -lihod or -lihed combined a lyke- form with had; spellings varied widely and no single standard existed.
items.cn: 中古英语的 -lihod、-lihed 把 lyke 一类词形与 had 结合，拼法十分多样，并没有单一标准。

items.en: The modern spelling likelihood is recorded in the fifteenth century, though the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代拼写 likelihood 在十五世纪已有记录，但确切的首见年代存疑。

items.en: Likely first named what looked promising or plausible, and likelihood kept that outward-looking sense before probability took the central place.
items.cn: likely 最初指「看起来有希望或可信」的事，likelihood 先保留这种外向的观感，之后「概率」义才占据中心。

items.en: Modern English uses likelihood mainly for chance, especially in the phrase in all likelihood.
items.cn: 现代英语中 likelihood 主要用于表示几率，尤其见于短语 in all likelihood。

note.en: The first group gathers the like family that supplies the base and its endings; the second gathers nouns for chance and the patterns of statistical prediction.
note.cn: 第一组收提供词基与词尾的 like 词族；第二组收表示几率以及统计预测模式的词。

entries.definition: The adjective that carries the core sense of being probable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「很可能的」，是承载核心含义的基础词。

entries.definition: A rarer noun with the same meaning as likelihood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，与 likelihood 同义，但使用较少。

entries.definition: The original word for being similar; it gave the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 原义为「相像」的词，整个词族都由它而来。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不太可能」，由否定前缀加本词构成。

entries.definition: The mathematical or formal measure of how likely an outcome is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「概率」，对结果有多大可能的数学或正式度量。

entries.definition: A chance that something may happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可能性」，某事可能发生或属实的余地。

entries.definition: The chances of something happening, often expressed as a ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「几率」，常以比例形式表示。

entries.definition: The statistical tool that scores how well a model explains observed data.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学名词，义为「似然函数」，衡量模型对观测数据的解释程度。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the like base, the noun ending -hood, and the fixed phrases; the abstract hooks picture clouds gathering over a city on a weather map.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 like 词基、名词后缀 -hood 与固定搭配；抽象记忆点想象云图上云层在城市上方聚拢。

normal.en: Likelihood is simply likely plus -hood, the same noun ending as in childhood.
normal.cn: likelihood 就是 likely 加 -hood，与 childhood 用的是同一个名词后缀。

normal.en: The likelihood of something is the most common pattern: the likelihood of rain.
normal.cn: the likelihood of 是最常见的结构：the likelihood of rain 即「下雨的可能性」。

normal.en: In all likelihood is a fixed phrase meaning almost certainly.
normal.cn: in all likelihood 是固定短语，意为「十有八九」。

normal.en: The base like means similar, so likelihood measures how much an event resembles its usual course.
normal.cn: 词基 like 意为「相像」，所以 likelihood 衡量一件事与它平常走向有多像。

normal.en: Verbs that often precede it are increase, reduce, and maximize the likelihood.
normal.cn: 常放在它前面的动词有 increase、reduce 与 maximize。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with storm clouds pressing one pan down and clear sky lifting the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，一端被乌云压下，另一端被晴空抬起。

abstract.en: Picture a forecaster drawing the same cloud line a little closer every hour.
abstract.cn: 想象预报员每小时把那条云带线往前挪一点。

abstract.en: Picture a small ribbon floating between yes and no, leaning slowly toward yes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细丝带悬在「会」与「不会」之间，缓缓倒向「会」。

examples.en: The likelihood of flooding rises after three days of rain.
examples.cn: 连续降雨三天之后，发生洪水的可能性会上升。

examples.en: In all likelihood, the hearing will be postponed until next month.
examples.cn: 十有八九，听证会将推迟到下个月。

examples.en: Researchers try to reduce the likelihood of errors in the data.
examples.cn: 研究人员设法降低数据出错的几率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克利」——来客越是常来，这件事发生的可能性就越大；likelihood 就是可能性。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自重构词根 lika-（身体、形状）；古英语 gelic（相像）与抽象后缀 -lic 构成基础词 likely，再加古英语 -had（状态）形成 -hood；核心义是「看起来像某事的程度」，本词没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from an everyday guess about what will happen, to a measured probability, to the promise a plan holds out.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从日常对「会不会发生」的猜测，走到可测量的概率，最后是方案所展现的希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: storm clouds pressing down one pan of a balance while the other stays high.
core.cn: 核心意象：乌云把天平一端压下，另一端高高悬着。

branches.en: The everyday guess about what will happen.
branches.cn: 日常对「会不会发生」的猜测。

branches.en: The same guess expressed as a figure under a model.
branches.cn: 把同一个猜测放在模型下用数字表达。

branches.en: A plan that still looks worth backing.
branches.cn: 一个看起来仍值得支持的计划。

branches.en: Both chance and promise rest on how likely an outcome looks.
branches.cn: 几率与希望都建立在结果看起来有多可能之上。

branches.en: The informal guess and the formal figure differ only in precision.
branches.cn: 口语的猜测与正式的数字只差在精确程度。

intro.en: The noun joins the base rather than a prefix: likely supplies the sense of being probable, and the ending -hood turns it into an abstract noun of state.
intro.cn: 这个词不是靠前缀，而是靠词基构成：likely 提供「很可能」的含义，后缀 -hood 把它变成表示状态的抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the family is Germanic, built from the root for likeness and two native endings.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；它属于日耳曼语词汇，由表示「相像」的词根与两个本地后缀构成。

items.example: Like is the seed of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: like 是整个词族的种子。

items.meaning: having the body or form of
items.example: The ending -ly builds likely and friendly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 likely 与 friendly。

items.meaning: having a good chance of happening
items.example: Likely supplies the core sense.
items.exampleCN: likely 提供核心含义。

items.example: The suffix -hood forms childhood and likelihood.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -hood 构成 childhood 与 likelihood。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms likeliness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 likeliness。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unlikelihood.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unlikelihood。

items.meaning: a blended ending used in rare words
items.example: The ending in unlikelihood models itself on the noun.
items.exampleCN: unlikelihood 的词尾就是比照这个名词造出来的。

items.example: The ending -s forms likelihoods.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 likelihoods。

items.example: Odds is the everyday companion of likelihood.
items.exampleCN: odds 是 likelihood 的日常近邻。
