definition_zh: 石灰；用石灰处理；黏鸟胶；椴树；酸橙
definition_en: a white mineral made from heated limestone, a sticky substance from bark, a tree, or a small sour green citrus fruit
core_image: 一篮青翠的酸橙，旁边立着一堵刚刷白的石灰墙
scene: 果园边的矮墙刚用石灰刷得雪白，墙头的筐里盛满了青绿色的果子。She squeezed half a lime into her glass of water before setting off for the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 lime 表示「酸橙」（第 5 个义项：一种绿色、味酸的小柑橘果实）；句意为出发去海边之前，她往杯子里挤了半个酸橙。画面中的主要对象：刷白的矮墙、白灰桶、装满青绿果子的筐。

pos.zh: 石灰；生石灰；黏鸟胶；椴树；酸橙
用石灰处理；往皮毛上涂黏鸟胶

derivatives.zh: 由 lime 与 stone 构成的复合词，义为「石灰岩」，一种主要由碳酸钙组成的沉积岩
由 lime 加 -y 构成，义为「含石灰的；黏的」
由 lime 与 wash 构成的复合词，义为「石灰浆」，也可作动词表示刷石灰浆
由 lime 与词尾 -ade 构成，义为「酸橙汁饮料」
复合名词，义为「石灰岩溶蚀台地」，流水沿裂隙溶蚀石灰岩后形成的平缓台地

senses.title: Calcium oxide from heated limestone
senses.definition: a white caustic solid made by heating limestone, used in building and farming
senses.definitionCN: 将石灰石高温煅烧后得到的白色腐蚀性固体，用于建筑与农业
senses.example: The masons mixed lime with sand to make a soft white mortar.
senses.exampleCN: 泥瓦匠把石灰和沙子混合，调成一种柔和的白色灰浆。
senses.why: Old English lim meant lime used in building, taken from the same Latin source as limestone, so the mineral came first and gave the word its oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lim 指建筑用的石灰，与 limestone 同出拉丁语来源，因此矿物义最早出现，也构成了这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Birdlime smeared on twigs
senses.definition: a sticky substance spread on twigs to catch small birds
senses.definitionCN: 涂在树枝上捕捉小鸟的黏性物质
senses.example: In the old orchard, hunters spread lime on the branches.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧果园里，捕鸟人往树枝上涂黏鸟胶。
senses.why: The sticky substance was named for its likeness to mortar, so a second sense grew out of the first by way of texture.
senses.whyCN: 这种黏性物质因质地像灰浆而得名，第二个义项就是顺着「黏」这一特征从第一个义项长出来的。

senses.title: The linden tree
senses.definition: a graceful tree with heart-shaped leaves and fragrant pale flowers
senses.definitionCN: 枝叶优美、叶子呈心形、花小而香且颜色浅淡的树
senses.example: A lime tree shades the whole corner of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵椴树为广场的整个角落遮阴。
senses.why: Modern English lime as the name of a tree was reshaped from Middle English lind, and the resemblance to the mineral is only phonological.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语中表示树的 lime 由中古英语 lind 改写而来，它在读音上像表示矿物的那个词，只是巧合。

senses.title: The pale yellow-green colour of the fruit
senses.definition: a bright pale yellow-green colour
senses.definitionCN: 明亮而浅淡的黄绿色
senses.example: The kitchen walls are painted lime.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的墙刷成了酸橙绿。
senses.why: The colour sense takes its name straight from the fruit, since the bright green skin is what the eye remembers.
senses.whyCN: 颜色义直接借自果实，因为人眼记住的正是那明亮的绿色果皮。

senses.title: The small sour green citrus fruit
senses.definition: a small green citrus fruit with a sharp sour taste
senses.definitionCN: 一种小而绿、味道尖酸的柑橘类果实
senses.example: Squeeze a lime into the soup before serving it.
senses.exampleCN: 上汤之前挤一个酸橙进去。
senses.why: The fruit sense came in by sea during the eighteenth century and merely borrowed the spelling of the older words; its family history is separate.
senses.whyCN: 果实义在十八世纪经海路传入，只是借用了更早那些词的拼写；它的词族历史是另一条线。

intro.en: Lime is several distinct words that share one spelling: the mineral from a Latin source, the sticky birdlime and the linden tree from older Germanic words, and the citrus fruit borrowed by sea in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: lime 是几个词共用一种拼写：矿物义源自拉丁语，黏鸟胶与椴树义来自更早的日耳曼语词，柑橘果实义则是十八世纪经海路借入的。

items.en: The Arabic word laymun named the citrus fruit and reached Spain with Arabic-speaking settlers.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 laymun 指柑橘类果实，随讲阿拉伯语的移民传到西班牙。

items.en: Spanish lima for limetta, the sweet lime, then passed into French and Portuguese.
items.cn: 西班牙语 lima 指甜柠檬，随后又传入法语与葡萄牙语。

items.en: The Provencal form limo carried the fruit name northward through Mediterranean trade.
items.cn: 普罗旺斯语形式 limo 借助地中海贸易把果实名带向北方。

items.en: This is the source of the mineral word, but it is a homonym, not a relative: Latin limus meant slime or mud, and had no connection with fruit.
items.cn: 这是矿物义的来源，但它只是一个同形词，而非亲属词：拉丁语 limus 意为淤泥、黏液，与果实毫无关系。

items.en: Old English lim meant lime the builder uses; the linden tree came from a separate Old English lind and the sticky birdlime from lim.
items.cn: 古英语 lim 指建筑用的石灰；椴树来自另一个古英语词 lind，黏鸟胶则来自 lim。

items.en: English lime was borrowed again for the green citrus fruit in the eighteenth century, and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪再度借入 lime 来指这种绿色柑橘果实，确切的首见年代存疑。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds and relatives of the mineral, the tree, and the fruit; the second gathers the building materials and citrus fruits that sit closest to it.
note.cn: 第一组收矿物、树木与果实的复合词及亲属词；第二组收与它最接近的建筑材料与柑橘类水果。

entries.definition: The calcium carbonate rock from which lime is made.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石灰岩」，烧制石灰所用的碳酸钙岩石。

entries.definition: A slang word for a British sailor or British person, from the lime juice the navy issued.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，俚语，指英国水兵或英国人，源自英国海军配发的酸橙汁。

entries.definition: The tree English speakers also call lime, with wider heart-shaped leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指英语中同样叫 lime 的椴树，叶子更宽的心形。

entries.definition: A drink made from lime juice, sugar, and water.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸橙汁饮料」，由酸橙汁、糖与水调成。

entries.definition: A dazzling light made by burning lime, or the state of public attention.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石灰光」，也指「公众关注的焦点」。

entries.definition: The paste of sand, water, and lime or cement that holds bricks together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灰浆」，由沙、水和石灰或水泥调成，用来黏合砖块。

entries.definition: The larger yellow citrus fruit with a similar sharp sourness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「柠檬」，与酸橙相近但更大、呈黄色的柑橘果实。

entries.definition: A climbing evergreen; birdlime was once smeared on stems and branches to catch birds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「常春藤」，一种攀爬的常绿植物；黏鸟胶曾被涂在茎与树枝上捕鸟。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks separate the mineral, the sticky glue, the tree, and the fruit, because they are separate words; the abstract hooks picture a white wall beside a basket of green fruit.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点把矿物、黏胶、树木与果实分开记，因为它们本是不同的词；抽象记忆点想象一面白墙旁边放着一篮绿果。

normal.en: Lime the mineral is calcium oxide, made by burning limestone.
normal.cn: 矿物义的石灰是氧化钙，由煅烧石灰岩得到。

normal.en: Lime the tree is what Americans call linden; the tree and the mineral share no history.
normal.cn: 树义的 lime 就是美式英语里的 linden，树与矿物没有任何渊源关系。

normal.en: The green citrus fruit was borrowed into English in the eighteenth century and merely reused the spelling.
normal.cn: 绿色的柑橘果实义在十八世纪借入英语，只是沿用了旧有的拼写。

normal.en: Slaked lime is quicklime that has been softened with water.
normal.cn: slaked lime（熟石灰）是加水和过的生石灰。

normal.en: Lime, like lemon, is a citrus word, and both end in the family ending -ade in fizzy drinks.
normal.cn: lime 与 lemon 都是柑橘词，在汽水名称里都带词尾 -ade。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of dark green fruit on a wall of fresh white wash.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮深绿色的果子摆在刚刷白的墙边。

abstract.en: Picture a stonemason sponging soft white lime onto a brick wall.
abstract.cn: 想象石匠用海绵把柔软的白色石灰抹上砖墙。

abstract.en: Picture a child skipping under a lime tree whose leaves make the square cool.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在椴树下跳绳，树叶把广场遮得清凉。

examples.en: Builders used lime and sand to make the old mortar.
examples.cn: 建筑工人用石灰和沙子调成那种老式灰浆。

examples.en: A slice of lime gives the water a sharp taste.
examples.cn: 一片酸橙让这杯水带上尖酸的味道。

examples.en: The farmer limed the field to reduce the acidity of the soil.
examples.cn: 农夫往田里施石灰，以降低土壤的酸度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莱姆」——一篮酸橙旁边立着一面刷白的石灰墙，青绿与雪白摆在一起；lime 既有酸橙，也有石灰。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 这是一个多源同形词：石灰义经古英语 lim 与拉丁语或日耳曼语来源相关联（更早来源不确定）；黏鸟胶义来自古英语 lim；椴树义来自古英语 lind；酸橙义十八世纪经西班牙语 lima、普罗旺斯语 limo 借入，最终追溯到阿拉伯语 laymun。几路来源在拼写上会合，彼此并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The senses divide along the old split: a white mineral sense, a sticky glue, a tree, and a colour, with the green fruit arriving last by sea.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项沿着历史上的分岔展开：白色矿物、黏性胶、树与颜色，最后才是经海路到来的绿色果实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of green fruit left standing beside a freshly whitened wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篮青绿果实放在刚刷白的墙边。

branches.en: The white caustic solid heated from limestone.
branches.cn: 由石灰岩煅烧得到的白色腐蚀性固体。

branches.en: The sticky twig smear that caught small birds.
branches.cn: 涂在树枝上捕捉小鸟的黏性物。

branches.en: The graceful tree that shades a whole corner.
branches.cn: 为一整个角落遮阴的优美树木。

branches.en: A colour named after the fruit, which was borrowed long after the other senses.
branches.cn: 以果实命名的颜色，而果实义比其他义项晚得多才借入。

branches.en: Mineral and glue are united by whiteness and stickiness, not by origin.
branches.cn: 矿物与黏胶之所以联在一起，靠的是白与黏，而不是同源。

intro.en: Lime is a short root rather than a prefixed word: the compounds limestone, limewash, limeade, and limelight are built by adding a second element, and the adjective limy adds -y.
intro.cn: lime 是一个短词根，而不是带前缀的词：limestone、limewash、limeade 与 limelight 都是加上第二个成分构成的，形容词 limy 则加 -y。

latinIntro.en: Latin limus is recorded here not as an ancestor of all the senses but as the source of the mineral word; the fruit came through Arabic laymun, which is outside the Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录拉丁语 limus，并不是说它是全部义项的祖先，而只是矿物义来源之一；果实义经阿拉伯语 laymun 而来，不在拉丁语族内。

items.example: Lime stands as a bare root.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个光秃秃的词根，不靠前缀而靠加第二个成分扩展。

items.example: The element -stone forms limestone.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -stone 构成 limestone。

items.example: The suffix -y forms limy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 limy。

items.meaning: to paint with a thin coating
items.example: The element -wash forms limewash.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -wash 构成 limewash。

items.meaning: a drink made from the base
items.example: The ending -ade forms limeade.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ade 构成 limeade。

items.example: The combining form lime- forms limelight.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 lime- 构成 limelight。

items.example: The element -light forms limelight.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -light 构成 limelight。

items.meaning: full of lime, then a slang name for the British
items.meaningCN: 含石灰的，后指英国人的俚称
items.example: Limey first meant lime-soaked.
items.exampleCN: limey 最初意为「浸过石灰的」。

items.meaning: an eye-formed modern name, unrelated in origin
items.meaningCN: 现代以眼睛形状相关的词，与本词不同源
items.example: Lyme appears in place names and has no link to lime.
items.exampleCN: Lyme 见于地名，与 lime 没有关系。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「石灰岩」
形容词，义为「含石灰的」
名词，义为「酸橙汁饮料」

definition_zh: 清澈的；透明的；明晰易懂的；平静安详的
definition_en: perfectly clear and free of any cloudiness, or easy to understand, or calm and untroubled
core_image: 浅滩上的水干净得能一眼看见水底的卵石
scene: 溪水浅处清得能看见每一块卵石的纹路，水面下连鱼鳞的反光都数得清。The stream was so limpid that we could count every stone on its bed.
sceneCN: 这里 limpid 是「清澈的」（第 1 个义项：水或液体清透、没有杂质）；句意为溪水如此清澈，我们能数清水底的每一块石头。画面中的主要对象：浅滩、卵石、水下闪光的鱼鳞。

pos.zh: 清澈的；透明的；明晰的；平静的

derivatives.zh: 由 limpid 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「清澈；明晰」
由 limpid 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「清澈地；明晰地」
由 limpid 加 -ness 构成，义为「澄清；明晰」，多与 limpidity 通用
形近但非同源的词，义为「无力的、松软的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同

senses.title: Clear water free of any cloudiness
senses.definition: so clear that objects can be seen through it without any cloudiness
senses.definitionCN: 清透得能看见其中的物体，没有任何浑浊
senses.example: The lake was limpid and the fish could be seen among the weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水清澈见底，水草间的鱼都看得清。
senses.why: The Latin source meant clear and transparent, most likely from lampas, a lamp of large clear stones, so limpid pictures water lit from within.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词意为「清澈透明的」，很可能来自表示大颗透亮宝石的 lampas（灯），因此 limpid 描绘的是水从里面透亮的样子。

senses.title: Easy to understand, often of writing or style
senses.definition: expressed clearly and simply, so that meaning shines through
senses.definitionCN: 表达得清楚简明，意思能一眼看透
senses.example: Her limpid prose makes a difficult argument easy to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 她明晰流畅的文章让一个艰深的论点易于理解。
senses.why: If seeing through water is clear seeing, then a style that lets meaning show through without effort is called limpid by the same move.
senses.whyCN: 既然看穿水面就是看得清楚，那么一种让意思不费力就透出来的文风，也就被同样的方式称为 limpid。

senses.title: Calm, untroubled, and serene
senses.definition: calm and untroubled, especially of a face, a mood, or a stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 平静无扰，尤指面容、心绪或一段时光
senses.example: He looked back on those years in a limpid mood.
senses.exampleCN: 回想那些年，他怀着平静安详的心情。
senses.why: Still water does not ripple and stays clear, so limpid extends from a quiet surface to a quiet state of mind.
senses.whyCN: 静止的水不起波纹、保持清澄，于是 limpid 从安静的水面延伸到安静的心境。

senses.title: The clear sound of a bell or a voice
senses.definition: clear, pure, and free of roughness, used of voices and ringing sounds
senses.definitionCN: 声音清亮纯净、不带粗糙，常用于形容嗓音与铃声
senses.example: The old bell had a limpid tone that crossed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那口旧钟音色清亮，传遍整个山谷。
senses.why: A clear medium lets light pass without scattering, and a clear sound passes the ear the same way, so the word crosses from sight to hearing.
senses.whyCN: 清澈的介质让光不被散射地通过，清亮的声音也以同样方式通过耳朵，于是这个词从视觉跨到了听觉。

senses.title: A lucid, transparent quality of mind
senses.definition: used of a mind or an analysis that sees things plainly and without confusion
senses.definitionCN: 形容头脑或分析看得分明、毫无混乱
senses.example: The book offers a limpid analysis of a tangled history.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对一段错综复杂的历史给出了透彻的分析。
senses.why: The image of transparent water is finally applied to thinking, because a clear mind shows matters the way clear water shows the stones.
senses.whyCN: 透明之水的意象最终被用在思维上，因为清晰的头脑呈现事物，就像清水呈现卵石。

intro.en: Limpid comes from French limpide, from Latin limpidus, clear or transparent; the further link to lampas, a bright lamp set with clear stones, is a common but not certain explanation.
intro.cn: limpid 来自法语 limpide，源头是拉丁语 limpidus（清澈、透明）；再往上与 lampas（镶透明宝石的明灯）相关联，是一种常见但未定的解释。

items.en: Latin limpidus meant clear, bright, and transparent, especially of liquids and of light.
items.cn: 拉丁语 limpidus 意为清澈、明亮、透明的，尤用于液体与光线。

items.en: One common explanation derives limpidus from lampas, a bright lamp or torch lit with large clear stones or gems; other accounts are less certain, so this link should be treated as probable rather than proved.
items.cn: 常见的解释认为 limpidus 源自 lampas（镶大颗透明宝石的明灯或火炬），但其他说法也存疑，因此这条联系只能视为可能而非定论。

items.en: Old French limpide carried the classical sense of clear and transparent into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 limpide 把「清澈透明」这一古典义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: English limpid has been recorded since the sixteenth century, initially for clear water and then for clear style.
items.cn: 英语 limpid 自十六世纪起有记录，最初用于形容清澈的水，随后用于明晰的文风。

items.en: Seventeenth-century criticism began to praise limpid prose, and the word moved firmly from liquids to language.
items.cn: 十七世纪的文学评论开始称赏明晰的文章，这个词便从液体稳稳移向语言。

items.en: Modern English keeps the water sense, extends it to calm moods and clear sounds, and uses limpidity for clearness in thought.
items.cn: 现代英语保留水的义项，把它扩展到平静的心绪与清亮的声音，并用 limpidity 表示思维的透彻。

note.en: The first group gathers words that look like limpid or share its Latin family; the second gathers the near-meaning words for water that can be seen through and for writing that can be followed.
note.cn: 第一组收与 limpid 形近或同属拉丁语词族的词；第二组收近义词，既有能看穿的水，也有易读的文章。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being limpid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「清澈；明晰」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning clearly and transparently.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「清澈地；明晰地」。

entries.definition: To walk with a lame step, or soft and drooping; just similar in letters, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跛行」，或形容词「松软的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Supple and able to bend easily; just similar in letters, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「柔软的、易弯曲的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A substance that flows, or flowing smoothly; just similar in letters, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「液体；流动的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Allowing light to pass through so that objects behind can be seen clearly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「透明的」，光线能穿过、能看清其后的物体。

entries.definition: Clear and easy to understand, especially of thought and writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「清晰易懂的」，尤用于思想与文章。

entries.definition: Free of anything that dims sight or understanding; the plainest word of the set.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「清楚的、清澈的」，这组词中最朴素的一个。

entries.definition: Very clear and easy to see through or follow, a more literary word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「清澈透明的、明了的」，更书面化。

entries.definition: Letting light through without showing shapes clearly, the weak contrast to limpid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「半透明的」，透光却看不清形状，恰与 limpid 形成对照。

entries.definition: Full of cloud or haze so that nothing can be seen through it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浑浊的、多云的」，什么都看不透，与 limpid 相反。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the lamp image behind limpidus and the switch from water to language; the abstract hooks picture a person standing in shallow water counting pebbles.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 limpidus 背后的「灯」意象，以及从水到语言的转移；抽象记忆点想象有人站在浅水里数卵石。

normal.en: Limpid is most likely linked to lampas, a lamp shining through clear stones, so the word carries its own light.
normal.cn: limpid 很可能与 lampas 有关，那是一盏透过透明宝石发光的灯，所以这个词自带光亮。

normal.en: Limpidity is the noun, limpidly the adverb, and both keep the water image.
normal.cn: limpidity 是名词，limpidly 是副词，二者都保留着水的意象。

normal.en: Limp and limber look close but are separate words, so keep them apart.
normal.cn: limp 与 limber 看着相近，却是另外的词，要把它们分开。

normal.en: Translucent lets light through but hides shapes, while limpid shows everything.
normal.cn: translucent 透光却挡形，limpid 则一切可见。

normal.en: A praise for style: limpid prose reads as if nothing stands between reader and meaning.
normal.cn: limpid prose 是对文风的褒奖，读来像读者与意思之间什么也没隔着。

abstract.en: Picture standing in shallow water and counting pebbles through it.
abstract.cn: 想象站在浅水里，隔着水数卵石。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp inside a glass bead that lights the table without a shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃珠里的一盏灯照亮桌面，不留阴影。

abstract.en: Picture a window with no dust at all, so the garden outside seems to be inside the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇一尘不染的窗，窗外的花园仿佛就在屋里。

examples.en: Mountain springs here are limpid and safe to drink.
examples.cn: 这里的山泉清澈见底，可以放心饮用。

examples.en: Her limpid style makes the report easy to read.
examples.cn: 她明晰流畅的文风让这份报告容易读。

examples.en: The stream flows limpid under the wooden bridge.
examples.cn: 小溪在木桥下清澈地流着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林辟的」——林中开出一条小径，一眼看到尽头，就像清水一眼看到底；limpid 就是清澈透明。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 limpidus（清澈、明亮、透明）→ 古法语 limpide → 英语 limpid；更早一般认为与 lampas（镶透明宝石的明灯）有关，但这条联系未完全确定；核心义是「光能毫无阻碍地透过」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with water showing everything beneath it, then move to clear style, to calm moods, to pure sounds, and to a mind that sees plainly.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项先用于显露一切的水，再转向清晰的文风、平静的心绪、纯净的声音，以及看得分明的头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shallow water so clear that the pebbles on the bed are counted one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅得能一块块数清水底卵石的清水。

branches.en: Water that hides nothing on its bed.
branches.cn: 水底什么也藏不住的水。

branches.en: Writing that lets the meaning show through.
branches.cn: 让意思透出来的文章。

branches.en: A still mood, as the still surface has no ripple.
branches.cn: 平静的心绪，正如静止的水面无波。

branches.en: Pure sounds and clear thinking both seem transparent.
branches.cn: 纯净的声音与清晰的思维都显得通透明亮。

branches.en: Both the water and the prose share the light and reveal what lies inside.
branches.cn: 清水与好文章一样，都让光透过去，显出里面的东西。

intro.en: Limpid is a bare Latin stem, not a prefixed word: the endings -ity, -ness, and -ly turn it into other parts of speech, and limp- is a look-alike stem met by chance.
intro.cn: limpid 是一个光裸的拉丁词干，并非带前缀的词：词尾 -ity、-ness 与 -ly 把它变成别的词类，而 limp- 只是外形相同的另一个词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin limpidus is the direct source, and lampas, the lamp, is the probable relative behind it; both are recorded here with a note on how certain each link is.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 limpidus 是直接来源，而 lampas（灯）是它背后可能的亲属词；这里两条都作了记录，并注明联系的确定程度。

items.example: The stem limp- carries the clear image.
items.exampleCN: 词干 limp- 承载「清澈」的意象。

items.example: The ending -id forms limpid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 构成 limpid。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms limpidity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 limpidity。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms limpidness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 limpidness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms limpidly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 limpidly。

items.example: The ending -ous appears in its relative pellucid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 出现在亲属词 pellucid 中。

items.example: The ending -ent appears in its relative transparent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 出现在亲属词 transparent 中。

items.example: The ending -escent appears in its relative translucent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -escent 出现在亲属词 translucent 中。

items.example: The same letters appear in limp and limber without a link.
items.exampleCN: 同样的字母出现在 limp 与 limber 中，却并无关联。

latinEntries.meaning: a bright lamp of clear stones
latinEntries.meaningCN: 镶透明宝石的明灯，仅为可能来源

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「清澈；明晰」
副词，义为「清澈地；明晰地」
名词，义为「澄清；明晰」

definition_zh: 亚麻布；亚麻织物；亚麻色的；床单类白色织物
definition_en: cloth woven from flax, the household articles made from it, and a pale greyish cream like new cloth
core_image: 一块刚洗过、在绳上晾着的白亚麻布，被风吹得发硬
scene: 夏日的民宿里，客人发现床单和枕套都是用同一种挺括的白布做成的，摸上去凉爽而略带纹理。The guest notices that the sheets and pillowcases are all cut from fresh white linen.
sceneCN: 这里 linen 是「亚麻布做的床单类织物」（第 2 个义项：用亚麻布缝制的家用品）；句意是客人发现床单和枕套都是用簇新的白亚麻布裁成的。布面那点纹理与凉感，就是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 名词：亚麻布；亚麻织物
名词：亚麻布制家用品（床单、桌布、餐巾）
形容词：亚麻色的；亚麻制的

derivatives.zh: 由 linen 与 fold（折叠处）复合而成，指旧宅中用来收纳亚麻织物的壁橱
共享同一词根的复合词，字面为「亚麻的种子」，义为「亚麻籽」
源自拉丁语 linum（亚麻）加 oleum（油），最初指用亚麻油制成的油地毡
由 linen 缩略形 linsey 与 wool 复合而成，义为「亚麻与羊毛混纺的粗布」，也喻指混杂不清的东西

senses.title: Cloth woven from flax
senses.definition: a strong cloth made from the fibres of the flax plant, woven into sheets and garments
senses.definitionCN: 用亚麻植物纤维织成的结实布料，可做成床单与衣物
senses.example: The table was covered with a white linen cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上铺着一块白色的亚麻桌布。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin linum for the flax plant, so linen is first of all the cloth those fibres become.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语中表示亚麻植物的 linum，所以 linen 首先指那些纤维织成的布。

senses.title: Household articles of that cloth
senses.definition: the sheets, tablecloths, and towels a household keeps as a set
senses.definitionCN: 家庭成套备置的床单、桌布与毛巾等织物
senses.example: She keeps the spare bed linen in the top cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 她把备用的床上织物放在最上面的柜子里。
senses.why: Since the oldest linen in a home was bedding, the material name came to stand for the things a household stores.
senses.whyCN: 旧时家里用得最多的亚麻物件就是寝具，于是材料名渐渐代指家庭成套储备的织物。

senses.title: A pale cream colour
senses.definition: a pale, slightly warm cream shade like untreated new cloth
senses.definitionCN: 像未染色的新布那样略带暖调的浅米色
senses.example: The walls were painted a soft linen shade.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁刷成柔和的亚麻色。
senses.why: Washed flax cloth keeps this natural cream tone, so the fabric lent its name to the colour.
senses.whyCN: 清洗过的亚麻布正是这种天然米色，于是织物的名字变成了颜色的名字。

senses.title: Of the nature of flax cloth
senses.definition: made of flax cloth, especially in describing garments for warm weather
senses.definitionCN: 用亚麻布制成，多用于描述适合温暖天气的衣物
senses.example: He wore a light linen jacket on the first day of summer.
senses.exampleCN: 入夏头一天他穿了一件轻薄的亚麻外套。
senses.why: As an attributive word linen turns from the stuff into a label for items made of it.
senses.whyCN: 作定语时 linen 从材料本身转成对材料制成之物的标注。

senses.title: The flax plant itself
senses.definition: the plant with blue flowers and slender stalks that yields these fibres
senses.definitionCN: 开蓝花、茎细长、提供这些纤维的植物
senses.example: Rows of linen grow close together in the northern fields.
senses.exampleCN: 北方田野里一垄垄亚麻长得很密。
senses.why: Before the word meant the cloth it named the plant, and that oldest sense still survives in rural use.
senses.whyCN: 在指布料之前，这个词指的是植物，最古老的那层意思在乡间用法里仍然存在。

senses.title: A setting for refined dining
senses.titleCN: 讲究的宴席；高级餐厅布设
senses.definition: an elegant table set with fine cloth, used as a symbol of formal hospitality
senses.definitionCN: 摆着精细布料的雅致餐席，用作正式待客的象征
senses.example: The evening called for white linen rather than a picnic blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 那个晚上需要的是铺白桌布的正席，而不是野餐毯。
senses.why: Fine cloth marks an occasion, so the material name has drifted into naming the whole formal setting.
senses.whyCN: 精细布料标志着场合的隆重，于是材料名转指整套正式的宴席陈设。

intro.en: Linen descends from Latin linum for the flax plant, through West Germanic and Old English lin, with the English ending added later. The deeper origin of linum is not established.
intro.cn: linen 可上溯到拉丁语中表示亚麻的 linum，经西日耳曼语与古英语 lin 传来，英语词尾则是后来加上的。linum 更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Linum meant flax, and its adjective lineus meant made of flax. The plant was widely grown around the Mediterranean.
items.cn: linum 意为亚麻，其形容词 lineus 意为亚麻制的。这种植物在地中海一带广为种植。

items.en: The source of linum before Latin is disputed; some scholars propose a non-Indo-European borrowing, but this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: linum 在拉丁语之前的来源有争议，有学者提出它借自非印欧语，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: A reconstructed form lin was borrowed from Latin into the West Germanic speech of the early centuries of our era.
items.cn: 一个重构形式 lin 在公元最初几世纪从拉丁语借入西日耳曼语。

items.en: Old English used lin for both the flax plant and its thread, and līnen as the adjective for things made of it.
items.cn: 古英语用 lin 兼指亚麻植物与亚麻线，并用形容词 līnen 表示亚麻制成的。

items.en: The adjective form with its endings became the noun, settling on linen for the cloth.
items.cn: 带词尾的形容词形式转成了名词，固定为 linen，指亚麻布。

items.en: Household linen and bed linen gave the colour name linen, and the word spread to textiles far beyond flax.
items.cn: 家用亚麻织物与床上织物又带来表示颜色的 linen，这个词也扩展到远远超出亚麻的纺织品。

note.en: The first group holds the spelling neighbours and flax relatives, the second the cloth names that linen is mistaken for.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近的词与亚麻同族词，第二组收容易与 linen 混淆的布料名称。

entries.definition: A ship or an aircraft of a scheduled line, or a removable inner layer.
entries.definitionCN: 定期航行的班轮、航班，或可拆的内衬。这个词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A long thin mark, or a row of things.
entries.definitionCN: 细长的线，或一排物体。字母与 linen 开头相同，但来源不同。

entries.definition: The plant whose fibres are woven into linen.
entries.definitionCN: 其纤维被织成亚麻布的植物，即亚麻；与 linen 指同一植物，但分属两个词。

entries.definition: Cloth woven from the fibres surrounding cotton seed.
entries.definitionCN: 用棉花种子周围的纤维织成的布；最常见的替代纤维。

entries.definition: Any woven or knitted material.
entries.definitionCN: 任何织成或编成的材料，是 linen 的上位词。

entries.definition: A heavy plain cloth used for sails and tents.
entries.definitionCN: 做帆与帐篷的厚重平纹布，与亚麻布同类但更粗。

entries.definition: A decorative fabric, originally of silk or linen, with a woven pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 最初用丝或亚麻织成、带有织纹的装饰性布料。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin plant word, the English family forms, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语植物名、英语同族形式，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: linen, line, and linseed all share the Latin plant name linum.
normal.cn: linen、line（亚麻线）与 linseed 都共享拉丁语植物名 linum。

normal.en: Flax is the plant; linen is the cloth woven from it.
normal.cn: flax 是植物，linen 是用它织成的布。

normal.en: Bed linen and table linen are the sets people store in a cupboard.
normal.cn: bed linen 与 table linen 是人们存在柜子里的成套织物。

normal.en: A linen suit is chosen for heat because the cloth breathes and dries fast.
normal.cn: 天热时选亚麻西装，因为这种布透气又干得快。

normal.en: Linen clothes crease easily, so an ironed linen shirt signals care.
normal.cn: 亚麻衣服容易起皱，所以熨平的亚麻衬衫表示用心打理。

abstract.en: Picture a flax field at noon, blue flowers trembling above slender stalks.
abstract.cn: 想象正午的亚麻田，细茎之上蓝花轻颤。

abstract.en: See a cupboard opening on stacked white sheets, cool and slightly stiff.
abstract.cn: 想象柜门打开，里面是一摞摞挺括的白床单，触感微凉。

abstract.en: Hold a new cloth to the light: it is that pale warm cream called linen.
abstract.cn: 把新布举向亮处：那种淡淡的暖米色就叫亚麻色。

examples.en: Fresh linen smells faintly of soap and sunshine.
examples.cn: 刚洗好的亚麻织物带着一点肥皂和阳光的气味。

examples.en: The hotel changes its bed linen every second day.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每隔一天更换一次床上织物。

examples.en: Linen keeps the drink cool far longer than paper or plastic.
examples.cn: 亚麻布比纸或塑料更能让饮料长时间保持低温。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理您」——理平、熨顺您的亚麻布床单与衬衫：亚麻布；亚麻色

root: 拉丁语 linum「亚麻」+ 形容词后缀 -eus（lineus「亚麻制的」），经西日耳曼语 lin 传入古英语，古英语形容词 līnen 后来转成名词；同族词有 line（亚麻线）、linseed、linoleum。linum 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses grow from one fibre: the cloth first, the household sets it furnishes, the natural colour it shows, its use as a label for garments, the plant that yields it, and finally the formal table it signals.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都从一种纤维长出来：先是布本身，再是布做成的家用成套织物、布天然的颜色、作定语标注衣物、提供纤维的植物，最后是布所标示的正式宴席。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white flax sheet drying on a line, stiff and cool to the touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳上晾着的白亚麻布，挺括而微凉。

branches.en: PLANT LINE: the field and the cloth are two ends of one fibre.
branches.cn: 植物线：田里的亚麻与身上的布是同一种纤维的两端。

branches.en: CUPBOARD LINE: the cloth becomes the sets a household keeps.
branches.cn: 柜子线：布变成了家庭成册储备的织物。

branches.en: COLOUR LINE: the natural tone of new cloth turns into a colour name.
branches.cn: 颜色线：新布的自然色调变成了颜色名。

branches.en: GARMENT LINE: the material becomes a label for summer clothes.
branches.cn: 衣物线：材料本身转成夏季衣物的标签。

branches.en: TABLE LINE: fine cloth turns storage into a symbol of hospitality.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：精细的布把储物变成了待客的象征。

intro.en: Linen is a bare stem from Latin linum, with the English -en ending inherited from the old adjective; its relatives are line, linseed, and linoleum.
intro.cn: linen 是源自拉丁语 linum 的裸词干，词尾 -en 承自旧的形容词；同族词有 line、linseed、linoleum。

latinIntro.en: Latin linum names the flax plant, -eus marks what is made of it, and English built linen, line, and linen-cloth from that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linum 指亚麻植物，-eus 表示「由……制成」，英语在此词干上造出 linen、line 与 linen-cloth。

items.example: Linum gives the whole family its stem.
items.exampleCN: linum 为整个词族提供词干。

items.example: Lineus is the model for the English adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: lineus 是英语形容词义的范本。

items.example: The suffix -eus forms lineus from linum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eus 由 linum 构成 lineus。

items.example: The ending in -en came from this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 来自这个古英语形容词。

items.example: The ending -en survives in the adjective linen.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 保留在形容词 linen 中。

items.example: Line is the short form of the same stem.
items.exampleCN: line 是同一词干的简短形式。

items.example: Linseed joins lin and seed.
items.exampleCN: linseed 由 lin 与 seed 合成。

items.example: Linoleum joins Latin linum and oleum.
items.exampleCN: linoleum 由拉丁语 linum 与 oleum 合成。

items.example: Flax names the plant that linen comes from.
items.exampleCN: flax 指产出亚麻布的植物。

definition_zh: 逗留；徘徊；（气味、感觉）持续；（目光）流连；（病人）苟延
definition_en: to stay in a place or state longer than expected, as when walking away slowly or when a smell or feeling refuses to fade
core_image: 最后一个客人已经穿好外套，手扶门框，还回过头多说一句
scene: 博物馆闭馆的音乐已经响起，可还有一对游客站在一幅画前，迟迟不肯挪步。After the closing bell, two visitors lingered in front of the painting.
sceneCN: 这里 linger 是「逗留、徘徊」（第 1 个义项：在该离开时仍不离开）；句意是闭馆铃响后，两位游客还站在画前停留。手扶门框、舍不得走的那副姿态，就是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 动词：逗留；徘徊；（气味等）持续不散
动词：（目光、心思）流连于；（疾病）久久不愈

derivatives.zh: linger 加 -ing 构成，义为「拖延的；久久不去的」，如 lingering doubt
linger 加 -er 构成，义为「磨蹭着不走的人」
lingering 加 -ly 构成，义为「拖拖拉拉地；久久地」
lingerer 的复数形式，义为「一群磨蹭着不走的人」

senses.title: To stay longer than necessary
senses.definition: to remain in a place instead of leaving, often because one does not want to go
senses.definitionCN: 待在某处而不离开，常因为不想走
senses.example: We lingered outside the cafe until the stars came out.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在咖啡馆门外待到星星出来还不肯走。
senses.why: The word behind linger means to prolong or to dwell, so the first picture is a person stretching out a stay.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的来源词意为拖长、停留，所以第一幅画面就是一个人把停留的时间拉长。

senses.title: Of a smell or feeling, to persist
senses.definition: of a smell, taste, or feeling, to stay present and fade only slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指气味、味道或感觉仍然存在，只是缓慢消退
senses.example: The smell of wood smoke lingered in our coats.
senses.exampleCN: 木柴烟的气味在我们的外套上久久不散。
senses.why: If a person can linger, anything that refuses to disappear can linger too, and smells are the first to do so.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以迟迟不走，任何不肯消失的东西也可以 linger，气味最先如此。

senses.title: Of a look, to rest on something
senses.definition: of the eyes or the mind, to rest on something and be slow to move away
senses.definitionCN: 指目光或心思停驻在某物之上，舍不得移开
senses.example: Her eyes lingered on the old photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目光在那张旧照片上流连。
senses.why: The same delay that keeps a body in a doorway can keep the eyes on a face or a page.
senses.whyCN: 把身体留在门口的那种停留，也能把目光留在一张脸或一页纸上。

senses.title: To walk or eat slowly
senses.definition: to go slowly or spend a long time over something pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢走，或在一件愉快的事上花很长时间
senses.example: He lingered over his coffee, watching the street wake up.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢啜着咖啡，看着街道醒过来。
senses.why: A slow pace is simply staying put in motion, the same reluctance to finish.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢其实就是在运动中的停留，是同一种舍不得结束。

senses.title: Of an illness, to drag on
senses.definition: of a disease or a weak life, to continue slowly and not end
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或衰弱的生命缓慢延续而不结束
senses.example: The fever lingered for another week.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧又持续了一个星期。
senses.why: A sickness that will not leave behaves like a guest who will not leave, so the verb shifts from people to conditions.
senses.whyCN: 不肯离去的病正像不肯离去的客人，于是这个动词从人身上转到状况上。

senses.title: To be left behind
senses.definition: to fall behind a group, or of a trace, to remain after the main thing is gone
senses.definitionCN: 指落在大队后面，或遗迹在主物消失后仍然留下
senses.example: Two latecomers lingered at the back of the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 两个迟到的人落在队伍的后面。
senses.why: Someone who stays when others move on is left behind, which is the passive side of the same delay.
senses.whyCN: 别人都走了而某人还留着，就是被落下，这是同一种停留的被动一面。

intro.en: Linger comes from Northern Middle English lengeren, a frequentative form of lengen meaning to prolong, which goes back to the Old English length word. The deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: linger 来自中古英语北方方言的 lengeren，是 lengen（拖长）的反复体形式，再上溯到古英语中表示「长度」的词。更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The English length word langung stood behind the root of this group, and a verb lengen meant to length out a thing.
items.cn: 这一词族的词根来自古英语表示「长度」的 langung，动词 lengen 意为把某物拉长。

items.en: Northern Middle English formed lengeren with the frequentative ending -er, meaning to keep dragging on, and lengeren became linger.
items.cn: 中古英语北方方言加上反复体词尾 -er，构成 lengeren，意为一再拖长，后来变成 linger。

items.en: The word first appears in northern writing meaning to delay or protract; the modern spelling is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 该词最早见于十四世纪的北方文献，意为拖延、延长；现代拼写自十六世纪有记载。

items.en: The frequentative form drove out the plain verb, and linger took over the sense of staying longer than one should.
items.cn: 反复体形式取代了原动词，linger 接过了「滞留过久」之义。

items.en: English extended the verb from people to smells, looks, and diseases, and to the related noun lingerie.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词从人扩展到气味、目光与疾病，还产生了同源名词 lingerie。

items.en: The deeper source of the length root is not established, and the shift from lengeren to linger cannot be fully explained by regular sound change.
items.cn: 「长度」词根更早的来源没有定论，从 lengeren 到 linger 的变化也无法完全用规则音变解释。

note.en: The first group holds the same-root and look-alike words, the second the staying and holding words that linger is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词与形近词，第二组收容易与 linger 混淆的停留类与持久类词。

entries.definition: Slow to end, or the act of staying on.
entries.definitionCN: 迟迟不结束的，或指逗留这一动作。

entries.definition: A person who stays behind when others leave.
entries.definitionCN: 别人走了还留下的人。

entries.definition: One of the long parts at the end of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 手末端的细长部分。这个词与 linger 只押韵，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To waste time or move slowly through carelessness.
entries.definitionCN: 因漫不经心而浪费时间或走得很慢。

entries.definition: To stand about in a place without a clear purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 无明显目的地在某处逗留；常带一点可疑的意味。

entries.definition: To live somewhere, or to keep one thought in mind.
entries.definitionCN: 居住，或反复琢磨某个念头。

entries.definition: To stick to a surface or to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于某个表面，或坚持某项规则。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Middle English frequentative form, the length root behind it, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的中古英语反复体形式、它背后的「长度」词根，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Linger comes from lengeren, a form of lengen meaning to prolong: the idea of stretching time out.
normal.cn: linger 来自 lengen（拖长）的反复体 lengeren，核心意思是把时间拉长。

normal.en: To linger is to lengthen a stay: the same length root hides at the back of the word.
normal.cn: linger 就是把自己的停留拉长，词根离「长度」不远。

normal.en: A lingering smell is a smell that will not end, from the same drawn-out idea.
normal.cn: lingering smell 是不肯结束的气味，同出「拖长」之意。

normal.en: Lingerie is not a garment of delay, but it comes from the same older word, with its own history.
normal.cn: lingerie 并非「拖延的衣服」，却出自同一旧词，另有自己的来历。

normal.en: Compare loiter: linger is gentle, loiter sounds aimless or suspicious.
normal.cn: 对比 loiter：linger 语气温和，loiter 听起来是无目的甚至可疑的逗留。

abstract.en: Picture a coat already on, a hand on the doorframe, one more sentence spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象外套已穿好、手扶着门框，还要再说一句话。

abstract.en: A drop of soup on a warm plate keeps sending up steam long after the bowl is empty.
abstract.cn: 空碗里的一小片汤渍在温热的盘子上，许久仍在冒热气。

abstract.en: See a tired eye travelling back to the same photograph on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一双疲倦的眼睛又一次回到桌上的同一张照片。

examples.en: He lingered at the bus stop long after his friends left.
examples.cn: 朋友们走后很久，他还在公交站逗留。

examples.en: A faint smell of coffee lingered in the empty kitchen.
examples.cn: 空厨房里还残留着淡淡一点咖啡味。

examples.en: Her cold lingered for weeks, refusing to clear.
examples.cn: 她的感冒拖了好几个星期都不见好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「零哥」——大家都散场了，零号座那位哥还坐着不走：逗留；徘徊

root: 中古英语北方方言 lengeren（一再拖长），是 lengen「使延长」的反复体形式，词根与古英语表示「长度」的 langung 同源；-er 为反复体词尾。更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses unfold from a stretched stay: the person who will not leave, the smell that will not fade, the eye that will not move, the slow pace, the illness that drags on, and the trace left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都从「被拉长的停留」展开：不肯离开的人、不肯散的气味、不肯移开的目光、缓慢的节奏、拖延的病，以及最后留下的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guest in a doorway, saying one more thing before going.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口的客人，走之前还要再多说一句。

branches.en: PLACE LINE: the body stays where it should have left.
branches.cn: 地点线：身体本该离开却留在原处。

branches.en: FADING LINE: smells and illnesses linger like guests who overstay.
branches.cn: 消退线：气味与病像不肯走的客人一样滞留。

branches.en: GAZE LINE: the delay moves from feet to eyes.
branches.cn: 目光线：停留从脚步转到了眼睛。

branches.en: PACE LINE: to linger is to stretch out motion itself.
branches.cn: 节奏线：linger 就是连运动本身也被拉长。

branches.en: RESIDUE LINE: staying on leaves something behind.
branches.cn: 残留线：停留过的人总会留下些什么。

intro.en: Linger is built on a native stem for length plus the frequentative -er, a native pattern rather than a Latin one.
intro.cn: linger 由本族语的「长度」词干加反复体词尾 -er 构成，属本族构词法而非拉丁构词法。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved in linger; the Latin word maneo, to remain, is suggested only as a semantic parallel, since English remain descends from it through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: linger 不涉及拉丁语成分；此处只把拉丁语动词 maneō（停留）作为语义对照列出，英语的 remain 正是经古法语由它而来。

items.example: Langung stands behind the length root of the verb.
items.exampleCN: langung 是这个词「长度」词根的来源。

items.example: The ending -er made older lengen into lengeren and later linger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把较早的 lengen 变成 lengeren，后来又成为 linger。

items.example: The ending -ing forms lingering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 lingering。

items.example: The suffix -er forms lingerer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 lingerer。

items.example: The ending -ed forms lingered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 lingered。

items.example: The ending -s forms lingers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 lingers。

items.example: The particle on forms linger on.
items.exampleCN: 小品词 on 构成 linger on。

items.example: The ending -ie turns linger into lingerie.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ie 把 linger 变成 lingerie。

definition_zh: 语言的；舌的；用舌头构成的；舌音的
definition_en: relating to language or to speech, and, in anatomy and phonetics, belonging to the tongue or produced with it
core_image: 发某个音时，舌尖轻轻抵住上齿龈的一瞬间
scene: 语音课上，老师让全班摸着自己的下巴发同一个辅音，体会舌面与齿龈接触的那一下，然后讲这种音在教材里的正式称呼。The teacher calls this consonant a lingual sound made at the back of the teeth.
sceneCN: 这里 lingual 是「舌的；用舌头构成的」（第 2 个义项：用于解剖与语音学的舌部义）；句意是朗读时留意舌尖与上齿后方齿龈的接触处。图中舌面触碰齿龈的那一下，就是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：语言的；言语的
形容词：舌的；用舌发音的；舌音的
名词：舌音

collocations.zh: 语言多元、多语并存的社会

derivatives.zh: lingual 加 -ly 构成，义为「在语言上；以舌部方式」
同一拉丁词根加 -istic 与 -s 构成，义为「语言学」
sub-（在下）加 lingual 构成，义为「舌下的」，如 sublingual gland
tri-（三）加 lingual 构成，义为「使用三种语言的」

senses.title: Relating to language
senses.definition: connected with language or with the use of speech, often in compounds with a prefix
senses.definitionCN: 与语言或言语使用有关的，常与前缀组成复合词
senses.example: The city supports bilingual and multilingual schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市支持双语与多语学校。
senses.why: Latin lingua named both the tongue and language, so the adjective built on it can describe whatever belongs to language.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lingua 兼指舌头与语言，由它构成的形容词自然也指一切属于语言的事物。

senses.title: Of the tongue, or made with it
senses.definition: in anatomy and phonetics, belonging to the tongue or produced by it
senses.definitionCN: 在解剖学与语音学中指属于舌头，或由舌头发出
senses.example: The dentist examined the lingual side of each tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医检查了每颗牙的舌面。
senses.why: Because lingua first meant the physical tongue, the same adjective keeps the bodily sense in medicine and phonetics.
senses.whyCN: 因为 lingua 本义就是有形的舌头，同一个形容词在医学与语音学里保留了身体义。

senses.title: A speech sound made by the tongue
senses.definition: a consonant articulated with the tongue, used as a noun in phonetics
senses.definitionCN: 用舌头发出的辅音，在语音学中作名词使用
senses.example: The older textbook lists the linguals among its consonant classes.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧教材把舌音列在辅音类别之中。
senses.why: The adjective takes on the noun role for the very sounds it describes, which is how phonetic labels become names.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词承担了名词角色，指它所描述的那类音，语音标签正是这样变成名称的。

senses.title: Shaped by the tongue in the mouth
senses.titleCN: 舌部的（由舌形成或贴近舌）
senses.definition: in dental or surgical description, on the side of the tongue or toward it
senses.definitionCN: 在牙科或外科描述中指靠近舌头那一侧，或朝向舌头
senses.example: A lingual shield keeps the device away from the tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 一种舌侧护片让装置不碰到舌头。
senses.why: The tongue as an organ has a side and a direction, and lingual marks both in technical description.
senses.whyCN: 作为器官的舌头有位置也有方向，lingual 在技术描述中同时标记这两点。

senses.title: Of spoken rather than written use
senses.definition: describing speech as it is actually voiced, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 描述实际说出口的语言，与书面相对
senses.example: The study compared lingual and written errors in students.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究比较了学生的口语错误与书面错误。
senses.why: Speech is the tongue in motion, so the organ word returns as a contrast with the pen.
senses.whyCN: 话语就是舌头在动，于是这个器官词又回来与笔相对。

intro.en: Lingual comes from medieval Latin lingualis, from lingua for tongue and language, with the Latin adjective ending -alis. The medieval form itself copies the earlier classical lines with the same ending. The deeper origin of lingua is uncertain.
intro.cn: lingual 来自中世纪拉丁语 lingualis，由指舌头与语言的 lingua 加拉丁形容词词尾 -alis 构成。中世纪这个形式本身也是照古典晚期同词尾的词形类推出的。lingua 更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Lingua named the tongue and, since the tongue makes speech, language as well; the adjective lingualis meant belonging to the tongue.
items.cn: lingua 指舌头，因为舌头能发出话语，也指语言；形容词 lingualis 意为属于舌头的。

items.en: The origin of lingua before Latin is disputed; a link with a verb for licking is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: lingua 在拉丁语之前的来源有争议，它与表示「舔」的动词有关只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Medieval Latin writers used lingualis for things of the tongue, including speech and, later, language in general.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语作者用 lingualis 指舌头相关之物，包括话语，后来又扩展到一般意义上的语言。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century, at first for the tongue as an organ of speech.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，最初用于指作为说话器官的舌头。

items.en: The plain adjective now feels rare, but it lives on in compounds: bilingual, trilingual, multilingual, and cross-lingual.
items.cn: 单独的形容词现在已少见，但它活了下来，见于 bilingual、trilingual、multilingual 与 cross-lingual 等复合词。

note.en: The first group holds the same-root words and the spelling neighbour, the second the language and speech words it is used alongside.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词与拼写相近词，第二组收与它一同使用的语言类、言语类词。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or one who speaks several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言的人，或通晓多门语言的人。

entries.definition: Relating to language or to the study of language.
entries.definitionCN: 与语言或语言研究有关的，是 lingual 的同族形容词。

entries.definition: Able to use two languages, made by adding the prefix bi-.
entries.definitionCN: 能用两种语言的，由前缀 bi- 加 lingual 构成。

entries.definition: Slow to end, staying on longer than expected.
entries.definitionCN: 迟迟不结束的。这个词只是开头相近，词源与 lingual 不同。

entries.definition: Relating to words, often to spoken words as opposed to written.
entries.definitionCN: 与词语有关，常指口头而非书面。

entries.definition: Spoken rather than written, or relating to the mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 口头的而非书面的，或与口部有关。

entries.definition: Relating to the voice or to speaking out.
entries.definitionCN: 与嗓音有关，或指直言表达。

entries.definition: Relating to speech sounds and how they are made.
entries.definitionCN: 与语音及其发音方式有关。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin lingua and the -alis ending, plus the compounds in which the word actually survives.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 lingua 与 -alis 词尾，以及这个词实际存身的复合词。

normal.en: lingual is lingua plus -alis, the Latin ending for belonging to something.
normal.cn: lingual 就是 lingua 加 -alis，后者是拉丁语中表示「属于……」的词尾。

normal.en: Latin lingua meant tongue first and language second, so lingual covers both.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 先指舌头，后指语言，所以 lingual 兼顾两者。

normal.en: bilingual, trilingual, and multilingual all end in the same -lingual block.
normal.cn: bilingual、trilingual、multilingual 的结尾都是同一个 -lingual。

normal.en: In dentistry, the lingual surface of a tooth faces the tongue.
normal.cn: 牙科里牙的舌面 lingual surface 就是朝向舌头的那一面。

normal.en: Compare linguistic: linguistic is about the study, lingual is about the tongue or language in general.
normal.cn: 对比 linguistic：linguistic 偏「研究语言」，lingual 偏「舌头或一般语言」。

abstract.en: Picture only the tip of the tongue touching the ridge behind the upper teeth while a sound comes out.
abstract.cn: 只想象舌尖抵住上齿后方齿龈、同时发出一个音的那一瞬。

abstract.en: Set a bright light behind your front teeth and see the tongue-lit inner face of every tooth.
abstract.cn: 想象把灯光放在门牙后面，照亮每颗牙朝向舌头的那一面。

abstract.en: Hear the plural linguals as the oldest name for these tongue-made consonants, now kept mostly in textbooks.
abstract.cn: 把这些由舌发出的辅音唤作「舌音」，那是它们最老的称呼，如今多留在教材里。

examples.en: Bilingual schools in the region add a second language from the first year.
examples.cn: 这一地区的双语学校从第一年就加入第二语言。

examples.en: The teacher calls this consonant a lingual sound made at the back of the teeth.
examples.cn: 老师把这种在上齿后方发出的辅音称为舌音。

examples.en: Pre-lingual hearing loss happens before a child has learned to speak.
examples.cn: 语前听力损失发生在孩子学会说话之前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「灵瓜」——一开口，灵巧的舌头像是把话切成一片片瓜：舌头；语言

root: 拉丁语 lingua「舌头；语言」+ 形容词词尾 -alis（lingualis「属于舌头的」）；同根词有 linguistic、language、bilingual。lingua 更早来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses run from one organ: language in general, the tongue as anatomy, the tongue-made sound, the tongue-side of a tooth, and finally speech as opposed to writing.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都从一个器官展开：一般意义上的语言、作为解剖部位的舌头、由舌发出的音、牙齿朝向舌头的一面，最后是口语与书面之别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tip of the tongue touching the ridge behind the teeth.
core.cn: 核心意象：舌尖抵住上齿后方齿龈的一瞬。

branches.en: LANGUAGE LINE: what the tongue produces becomes a whole field of study.
branches.cn: 语言线：舌头产出的话语成了一大研究领域。

branches.en: ORGAN LINE: the body keeps the oldest sense, in dentistry and surgery.
branches.cn: 身体线：身体保留了最古老的义项，见于牙科与外科。

branches.en: SOUND LINE: the adjective turns into a name for a class of consonants.
branches.cn: 声音线：形容词转成某一类辅音的名称。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: what is said out loud against what is written.
branches.cn: 口语线：说出口的话与写下的字相对。

branches.en: COMPOUND LINE: bilingual and linguals both live on inside longer words.
branches.cn: 复合线：bilingual 与 linguals 都以更长的词形继续存活。

intro.en: Lingual is a Latin stem plus a Latin ending; English grows it with prefixes bi-, tri-, multi-, and sub-, and with the endings -ly and -ist.
intro.cn: lingual 是拉丁词干加拉丁词尾；英语用前缀 bi-、tri-、multi-、sub- 以及词尾 -ly、-ist 来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua means tongue and language, and the adjective lingualis adds -alis to show belonging, giving English lingual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 意为舌头与语言，形容词 lingualis 加 -alis 表示归属，正是英语 lingual 的来源。

items.example: Lingua supplies the whole stem.
items.exampleCN: lingua 提供整个词干。

items.example: Lingualis is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: lingualis 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -alis forms lingualis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -alis 构成 lingualis。

items.example: The prefix bi- forms bilingual.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 bi- 构成 bilingual。

items.example: The prefix tri- forms trilingual.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 tri- 构成 trilingual。

items.example: The prefix multi- forms multilingual.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 multi- 构成 multilingual。

items.example: The prefix sub- forms sublingual.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 构成 sublingual。

items.example: The ending -ly forms lingually.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 lingually。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms linguist from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 在同一词干上构成 linguist。

items.example: The ending -s forms linguals.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 linguals。

definition_zh: 语言学家；语言学研究者；精通语言（尤指多种外语）的人
definition_en: a specialist in linguistics, or a person skilled in the use of languages
core_image: 一个人俯身看着古老的文字铭文，把舌头与语言的秘密拆开、称量、记录
scene: 那位研究古铭文的学者在研讨会上被介绍为语言学家。The scholar who studies old inscriptions was introduced at the seminar as a linguistician.
sceneCN: 这里 linguistician 是「语言学家」（第 1 个义项：专门研究语言学的人）；句意：那位研究古铭文的学者在研讨会上被介绍为语言学家。

pos.zh: 语言学家；语言学研究者；通晓多语者

collocations.zh: 研究古典语言的语言学家

derivatives.zh: 由 linguist 派生、加 -ic 构成，义为「语言的；语言学的」
由 linguistic 加 -s 构成，义为「语言学」
由拉丁语 lingua 与 -ist 构成，义为「通晓多种语言的人；语言学家」
由 linguistic 加 -ally 构成，义为「在语言上；从语言学角度」

senses.title: A specialist in linguistics
senses.titleCN: 语言学家；语言学研究者
senses.definition: a person who studies language as an object of scientific analysis
senses.definitionCN: 把语言作为科学研究对象加以研究的人
senses.example: The linguistician traced the verb endings back to an older sound.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家把那些动词词尾追溯到更古老的一个音。
senses.why: The abstract noun linguistics, the study of language, plus the ending -ian yields its student.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词 linguistics 指对语言的研究，加上表示「从事者」的词尾 -ian，就得到了从事这项研究的人。

senses.title: A master of many tongues
senses.definition: a person skilled in several languages rather than in theory
senses.definitionCN: 擅长多种语言而非擅长语言理论的人
senses.example: The market traders relied on a linguistician who moved between six dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 市场商贩仰赖一位能在六种方言间自如切换的语言通。
senses.why: Latin lingua means tongue, and the word began as a learned name for someone skilful in tongues before theory took over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lingua 意为「舌头」，这个词最初是学问语，用来称呼擅长多种语言的人，后来才转向理论研究者。

senses.title: A writer on language questions
senses.titleCN: 研究语言问题并撰写论著的人
senses.definition: a scholar who writes on doubtful points of grammar, usage, or etymology
senses.definitionCN: 就语法、用法或词源中的疑难问题撰写论著的学者
senses.example: Nineteenth century journals printed many letters from a country linguistician.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的期刊刊登了许多来自一位乡间语言研究者的来信。
senses.why: Older usage often joined the word with a place name to describe a learned amateur who answered questions in print.
senses.whyCN: 较早的用法常把这个词与地名连用，指在报刊上解答问题的博学好古者。

intro.en: Linguistician joins the Latin word for tongue to the endings that name a student of a subject.
intro.cn: linguistician 把拉丁语中表示「舌头」的词与表示「某学科研习者」的词尾连在一起。

items.en: Lingua means tongue and language, and lingua, the thing that speaks, gave the stem lingu-.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头与语言，作为会说话的器官，它给出了词干 lingu-。

items.en: Linguist was borrowed from French to name a person skilled in languages.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语从法语借入 linguist，用来称呼擅长多种语言的人。

items.en: Linguistics is coined for the scientific study, and linguist shifts towards the scholar.
items.cn: 语言学作为学科被命名为 linguistics，linguist 逐渐偏向指学者。

items.en: Linguistician appears as a longer rival to linguist and to philologist.
items.cn: 作为 linguist 与 philologist 之外更长的变体，linguistician 出现。

items.en: The longer word survives in formal and archaising prose, while linguist stays standard.
items.cn: 这个较长的词保留在正式与仿古文字中，而 linguist 成为标准形式。

note.en: One group shares the tongue stem; the other holds the rival names for people who work on language.
note.cn: 第一组共享「舌头」词干；第二组是其他表示语言工作者的名称。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a person skilled in language or trained in linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，指擅长语言或受过语言学训练的人。

entries.definition: Relating to language or to the study of language.
entries.definitionCN: 与语言或语言研究有关的。

entries.definition: The subject itself, the scientific study of language.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身，对语言的科学研究。

entries.definition: A scholar of texts and languages studied historically, the older rival title.
entries.definitionCN: 研究文献与语言历史的学者，是较早的竞争称谓。

entries.definition: A person who can read or speak several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 能阅读或使用多种语言的人。

entries.definition: A specialist in grammar rather than in language as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻语法而非整体语言的专家。

normalIntro.en: Break the long word into language plus the person who studies it.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个长词拆成「语言」再加上「研究语言的人」。

normal.en: The ending -ian names the person, just as it does in musician and historian.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ian 表示人，就像在 musician 与 historian 中一样。

normal.en: Linguistics is the field, and the linguistician is the person inside it.
normal.cn: linguistics 是学科，linguistician 是学科中的人。

normal.en: The Latin stem lingua, tongue, also stands behind language, bilingual, and linguist.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词干 lingua（舌头）也存在于 language、bilingual 与 linguist 之中。

normal.en: The plural is linguisticians; a rare variant spelling drops the second i.
normal.cn: 复数是 linguisticians；另有少见变体拼写少一个 i。

normal.en: Modern textbooks prefer linguist, so treat this word as formal and old fashioned.
normal.cn: 现代教材多用 linguist，因此应把这个词看作正式且稍显古旧。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar leaning over a carved stone and sounding each old letter aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者俯身在刻字石碑前，把每个古字母都念出声。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller changing languages at every market stall before breakfast.
abstract.cn: 想象一位旅人在早餐前就能在每个摊位前换一种语言交谈。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of handwritten letters to a journal arguing about one doubtful word.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠寄给期刊的手写信，全都在争论同一个有疑问的词。

examples.en: A linguistician was invited to explain the sound change to the local society.
examples.cn: 一位语言学家受邀向当地学会解释这一音变。

examples.en: Two linguisticians disagreed over the origin of the suffix in the old dialect.
examples.cn: 两位语言学家对那个古老方言后缀的来源意见不一。

examples.en: The museum hired a trained linguist to catalogue the tablets.
examples.cn: 博物馆雇了一位训练有素的语言学家来编目那些泥板。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拎滚石头」——拎着滚烫的石头去研究古人刻的字，就是语言学家；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lingua（舌头；语言）→ linguist（通晓语言者）＋ -ic → linguistic（语言的）＋ -s → linguistics（语言学）＋ -ian（从事者）→ linguistician，核心义「研究语言的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The word names first the theorist of language, then the practical speaker of many tongues, and finally the learned writer who settles doubtful points of usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指语言理论研究者，再指实际通晓多种语言的人，最后指在报刊论著中辨析用法的博学作者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar bent over old letters, pulling language apart and naming each piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：学者俯身于古老文字，把语言拆开并逐一命名。

branches.en: The theorist of language is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 语言理论研究者是主要的现代义项。

branches.en: Skill in many tongues is the older practical sense.
branches.cn: 通晓多种语言是较早的实用义项。

branches.en: The published commentator on usage is the learned amateur sense.
branches.cn: 发表论述的用法评论者是博学好古的义项。

branches.en: Both describe someone who argues about doubtful forms in print.
branches.cn: 两者都描述在文字中争论疑难词形的人。

branches.en: Practice with many languages and theory about language often meet in one person.
branches.cn: 多种语言的实践与关于语言的理论常常汇于一人。

intro.en: Linguistician is a compound of the tongue stem and the suffix for a student of a field.
intro.cn: linguistician 由「舌头」词干与表示「某领域研习者」的后缀合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua means tongue and language, and its stem lingu- carries the idea of speech into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 意为舌头与语言，其词干 lingu- 把「言语」之意带入英语。

items.example: Lingu- is the fixed stem in the family.
items.exampleCN: lingu- 是这个词族固定的词干。

items.example: Lingua is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: lingua 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ic yields linguistic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 linguistic。

items.example: The ending -s in linguistics marks a disciplina.
items.exampleCN: linguistics 中的 -s 标记一门学科。

items.example: The suffix -ian makes the profession word.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ian 造出表示职业的词。

items.example: Linguist is the shorter standard word.
items.exampleCN: linguist 是更短的标准词。

items.example: The prefix bi- adds the number two.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 bi- 加入「二」的意思。

items.example: Linguistically turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: linguistically 把形容词变为副词。

items.example: The suffix -ist appears in linguist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 出现在 linguist 中。

definition_zh: （门或窗上方的）过梁；楣石；水平承重梁
definition_en: a horizontal beam or stone across the top of a door, window, or opening, carrying the weight above it
core_image: 一块长石横架在两座石柱顶端，把门洞上方整面墙的重量稳稳托住
scene: 石匠把一块长白石安放在门框上方，托住了整面墙的重量。The mason set a long pale lintel above the doorway, and it carried the weight of the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 lintel 是「门楣、过梁」（第 1 个义项：门窗上方的水平承重横梁）；句意：石匠在门口上方安放了一块浅色的长条过梁，它承托着墙的重量。

pos.zh: 过梁；楣石；（门窗上方的）水平横梁

derivatives.zh: 由 lintel 加 -ed 构成，义为「有过梁的；带楣石的」
由 post（立柱）与 lintel 复合而成，义为「梁柱式的（建筑结构）」
door 与 lintel 复合而成，义为「门楣」

senses.title: The beam over an opening
senses.definition: a horizontal member spanning the top of a door or window and supporting the structure above
senses.definitionCN: 横跨门窗顶部的水平构件，用来支撑其上方的结构
senses.example: A crack ran through the stone lintel above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方的石过梁裂了一道缝。
senses.why: The oldest architectural meaning is simply the beam that lets a wall carry on over a gap.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的建筑学含义就是让墙体能够跨过缺口继续向上的那根梁。

senses.title: The carved face of a doorway
senses.definition: the decorated face of that beam, often carved with names, signs, or figures
senses.definitionCN: 横梁朝向门外的装饰性表面，常刻有名字、符号或图案
senses.example: The carved lintel announced the owner family in old script.
senses.exampleCN: 镌刻的门楣用古文字表明主人家族。
senses.why: Because it faces every visitor at eye level, the lintel became the natural place for inscription and ornament.
senses.whyCN: 因为它正对每位来客、与视线齐平，门楣自然成为铭文与装饰的位置。

senses.title: Any horizontal span in construction
senses.definition: a general construction term for a horizontal member bridging two supports, as in tunnels and metal frames
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与工程中泛指跨越两个支撑的水平构件，如隧道与金属框架中所用
senses.example: Engineers replaced the damaged lintel in the tunnel portal.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师更换了隧道口受损的过梁。
senses.why: Modern building practice kept the old noun and applied it to steel and concrete spans of the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 现代建筑沿用了这个旧名词，把它扩展到形状相同的钢梁与混凝土跨度构件上。

intro.en: Lintel most likely descends from a Latin word for the threshold, shaped by Old French building speech.
intro.cn: lintel 最可能源自拉丁语中表示「门槛」的词，经古法语建筑用语塑形。

items.en: Limes means threshold, and its diminutive liminare names the sill or the outer opening.
items.cn: limes 意为门槛，其指小形式 liminare 指门槛或门口外围。

items.en: Building speech changes the initial m to n, giving forms around lintel and linteau.
items.cn: 建筑用语把开头的 m 变成 n，得到 lintel、linteau 一类形式。

items.en: Lintel enters English as the name of the beam over a doorway.
items.cn: lintel 进入英语，指门洞上方的横梁。

items.en: Writers connect the word with linden, the lime tree, and claim wooden beams were cut from it.
items.cn: 十六世纪作者把它与 linden（椴树）联系起来，声称横梁取自椴木。

items.en: Scholars treat that tree link as a folk story, while the word spreads to steel and concrete spans.
items.cn: 学者认为那种「椴木」联系只是民间传说，同时该词扩展到钢梁与混凝土跨度构件。

note.en: The first group holds the other parts of an opening; the second holds general words for beams and arches.
note.cn: 第一组是门洞的其他构件；第二组是泛指梁、拱与水平构件的词。

entries.definition: The vertical side piece of a doorway that carries the lintel.
entries.definitionCN: 门洞两侧承受过梁的竖向立柱。

entries.definition: The horizontal piece at the foot of a window or door.
entries.definitionCN: 窗或门底部的水平构件。

entries.definition: Shared the Latin threshold word, not a beam.
entries.definitionCN: 与它共享拉丁语「门槛」一词，但并不是梁。

entries.definition: A general word for any horizontal structural support.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何水平结构支撑的通用词。

entries.definition: The curved span that replaces a lintel over an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 曲线形的跨度构件，可取代门洞上方的过梁。

entries.definition: The moulded band around a doorway, ornamental rather than load bearing.
entries.definitionCN: 门洞周围的线脚带，偏装饰而非承重。

normalIntro.en: Hold the beam picture: lintel is the top rail of a doorway, jambs are the sides.
normalIntro.cn: 记住横梁画面：lintel 是门口的顶梁，jamb 是两侧。

normal.en: Rhyme it with threshold: both words concern the edge of an opening.
normal.cn: 与 threshold 一起记：两者都涉及门洞的边缘。

normal.en: Stone lintel and wooden lintel are the two most common collocations.
normal.cn: 石过梁与木过梁是两个最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The plural is regular, lintels, and the adjective is lintelled.
normal.cn: 复数是规则的 lintels，形容词是 lintelled。

normal.en: Classical Greek temples show the flat lintel above the columns, which sit below it.
normal.cn: 古希腊神庙的柱子之上是平直的过梁。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with lentil, the pulse, though the two spellings nearly match.
normal.cn: 不要与 lentil（扁豆）混淆，虽然拼写几乎相同。

abstract.en: Picture a stone plank bridging two gateposts.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板横跨两根门柱。

abstract.en: Imagine a name carved at eye level above the door.
abstract.cn: 想象门上方与视线齐平处刻着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a steel bar holding up the mouth of a tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根钢梁撑起隧道洞口。

examples.en: The old stone lintel bore the date of the house.
examples.cn: 古老的门楣上刻着这座房子的建造日期。

examples.en: Builders replaced two wooden lintels with steel beams.
examples.cn: 建筑工人用钢梁替换了两根木过梁。

examples.en: Olive branches hung over the lintel during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间门楣上方挂着橄榄枝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林头」——森林里那根做门楣的大横木，就架在门口上头；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 limes（门槛）的指小形式 liminare → 古法语建筑用语中以 n 替换 m，形成 lintel 一类形式 → 中古英语 lintel，核心义「门洞上方的横梁」；与 linden（椴树）的联系仅为民间传说。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts as the beam over a gap, turns into the decorated face everyone sees, and widens into any horizontal span.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词起于跨过缺口的梁，转指众人可见的装饰性门面，再扩展为任何水平跨度构件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long stone laid across two posts, holding up the wall above.
core.cn: 核心意象：长条石块横架两根立柱之上，托住上方的墙体。

branches.en: The load bearing beam is the core architectural sense.
branches.cn: 承重横梁是核心的建筑义项。

branches.en: The carved front turns a support into a sign.
branches.cn: 雕刻的正面把支撑物变成标志。

branches.en: The engineering span is the widened technical sense.
branches.cn: 工程跨度构件是扩展的技术义项。

branches.en: Both name a horizontal member bridging two supports.
branches.cn: 两者都指跨越两个支撑的水平构件。

branches.en: The face of the beam is where ornament is placed.
branches.cn: 梁的正面正是装饰所在之处。

intro.en: Lintel is a whole borrowed noun from building French, with few productive pieces to split off.
intro.cn: lintel 整体借自法语建筑用语，能拆出的构词成分很少。

latinIntro.en: Latin limes means threshold, and the French building word reshaped it into the English beam noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 limes 意为门槛，法语建筑词把它改造成英语的梁名词。

items.example: Limin- survives in liminal, meaning on a threshold.
items.exampleCN: limin- 保留在 liminal（门槛的；过渡的）中。

items.example: Limes is the supposed distant source.
items.exampleCN: limes 是推测的远源。

items.example: The ending -el also appears in tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -el 也出现在 tunnel 中。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms lintelled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 lintelled。

items.example: Plural adds a plain s.
items.exampleCN: 复数直接加 s。

items.meaningCN: 最古老的梁柱框架体系
items.example: The compound names the upright and the span together.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把立柱与跨度合在一起命名。

items.example: Linden was wrongly linked to lintel by old writers.
items.exampleCN: 旧时作者把 linden 与 lintel 错误地联系起来。

items.example: Lentil is only a spelling twin of lintel.
items.exampleCN: lentil 只是 lintel 的拼写双胞胎。

definition_zh: 无精打采的；倦怠的；缺乏兴趣与干劲的
definition_en: having no energy or interest, and making little or no effort to act
core_image: 一个人整个人瘫在椅子上，肩膀下垂，眼睛望着远处，连抬手的念头都没有
scene: 整个下午他都瘫在椅子上，连书页都懒得翻。All afternoon he sat slumped in the chair, listless and unwilling even to turn a page.
sceneCN: 这里 listless 是「无精打采的」（第 1 个义项：没有精神与兴趣）；句意：整个下午他都瘫在椅子里，无精打采，连翻一页书都不愿意。

pos.zh: 无精打采的；倦怠的；缺乏兴趣的

derivatives.zh: 由 listless 加 -ly 构成，义为「无精打采地」
由 listless 加 -ness 构成，义为「疲倦消沉；缺乏兴致」
构成 listless 的那部分，古义「意愿；兴致」，与「清单」义无关

senses.title: Without energy or spirit
senses.definition: tired in a dull way, showing no liveliness or keenness
senses.definitionCN: 以迟钝的方式疲倦着，不显出活力与热心
senses.example: The child became listless after a night without sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子一夜没睡，变得无精打采。
senses.why: The suffix means without, and the old noun meant desire, so the word describes a person emptied of eagerness.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「没有」，旧名词意为「意愿」，因此这个词描述一个被抽空了热情的人。

senses.title: Indifferent, making no effort
senses.definition: showing no inclination to act or to try, because nothing seems worth the effort
senses.definitionCN: 因为觉得什么都不值得费力，所以不愿行动或尝试
senses.example: The audience grew listless and checked their phones.
senses.exampleCN: 观众变得倦怠，开始看手机。
senses.why: Indifference is the same lack of desire seen from outside, as a refusal to make an effort.
senses.whyCN: 冷漠是从外部看到的同一种「无意愿」，表现为不愿费力。

senses.title: Medicine: lacking alertness
senses.definition: used of a patient who is unusually dull and unresponsive over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 用于病人，指在一段时间内异常迟钝、反应淡漠
senses.example: A listless baby should always be seen by a doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 精神萎靡的婴儿一定要让医生看诊。
senses.why: Clinical notes borrowed the everyday word to describe a body with no spare energy left.
senses.whyCN: 临床记录借用了日常词，用来描述身体已无多余精力。

senses.title: Markets: dull and inactive
senses.definition: applied to trade, sport, or any activity that is slack and without life
senses.definitionCN: 用于贸易、体育或任何活动，指萧条而毫无生气
senses.example: Trading was listless ahead of the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节假日前交易清淡低迷。
senses.why: Business writing reuses the word for any system that shows no appetite to move.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个词挪用到任何提不起劲头去运转的体系上。

intro.en: Listless pairs list, an old word for desire, with the suffix -less, without.
intro.cn: listless 把表示「意愿」的古词 list 与后缀 -less（没有）组合起来。

items.en: A word best recorded as lystan means to please or to be desirable.
items.cn: 古英语用 lystan 这类形式表示「使愉悦」「令人中意」。

items.en: The noun list takes the sense of desire, pleasure, or inclination.
items.cn: 中古英语中名词 list 取得「意愿」「兴致」的含义。

items.en: The old phrase at ones list, meaning at pleasure or by inclination, is still in use.
items.cn: 短语 at ones list（凭其意愿、乘其兴致）仍在使用。

items.en: Listless is recorded as a word for having no desire or inclination.
items.cn: listless 作为「无意愿、无兴致」的词被记录下来。

items.en: The word settles into its modern sense of tired indifference and spreads to trade and medicine.
items.cn: 这个词固定为现代「疲倦而漠然」之意，并扩展到贸易与医学领域。

note.en: The first group shares the word for desire or the -less ending; the second gives other words for low energy.
note.cn: 第一组共享「意愿」词源或 -less 后缀；第二组给出其他表示情绪低落的词。

entries.definition: In old use, desire or inclination; not the modern catalogue.
entries.definitionCN: 古义为「意愿、倾向」，并非现代的「清单」。

entries.definition: A close relative naming strong desire, which survives with a stronger tone.
entries.definitionCN: 同源近亲，指强烈欲望，语气更重。

entries.definition: The adverb, naming how an action is done without energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，说明动作是以无精打采的方式进行的。

entries.definition: Slower and heavier than normal, often through illness or heat.
entries.definitionCN: 行动比平常迟缓沉重，常因疾病或炎热。

entries.definition: Soft and slack without being sad, used of gestures and air.
entries.definitionCN: 松弛绵软但不悲伤，多用于姿态与气氛。

entries.definition: Caring about nothing, a stronger claim about interest.
entries.definitionCN: 什么都不在乎，对「兴趣」的否定更强。

normalIntro.en: Read the word as list plus less: no desire left on the list.
normalIntro.cn: 把词读成 list 加 less：单子上已经没有任何愿望了。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without, as in careless and helpless.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 意为「没有」，如 careless 与 helpless。

normal.en: The old list meant desire, so listless is literally desire-less.
normal.cn: 古词 list 意为意愿，所以 listless 字面就是「无意愿」。

normal.en: The adverb is listlessly and the noun is listlessness.
normal.cn: 副词是 listlessly，名词是 listlessness。

normal.en: Compare lust, a cousin with the same root but a much hotter tone.
normal.cn: 对比 lust，它是同根近亲，但语气热烈得多。

normal.en: Doctors note a listless child; teachers notice a listless class.
normal.cn: 医生留意精神萎靡的孩子，老师留意倦怠的班级。

abstract.en: Picture someone sunk in an armchair with an unread book on the lap.
abstract.cn: 想象某人陷在扶手椅里，膝上摊着一本没读的书。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where nobody even lifts a hand to answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没人肯举手回答的会议。

abstract.en: Picture a feverish child lying with open eyes and no reaction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个发烧的孩子睁着眼睛躺着，毫无反应。

examples.en: The long meeting left everyone listless and silent.
examples.cn: 漫长的会议让所有人都无精打采、沉默不语。

examples.en: She felt listless for days after the illness.
examples.cn: 病后好几天她都感到倦怠无力。

examples.en: The players walked off the pitch with a listless expression.
examples.cn: 球员们带着倦怠的神情走下球场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累死了」——累到什么都不想干，就是 listless；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lystan（使愉悦；令人中意）→ 中古英语 list（意愿；兴致）＋后缀 -less（没有）→ listless，核心义「没有干劲」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a body without eagerness, then describes a refusal to make an effort, and finally spreads to patients and to markets.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起于没有热情的身体，进而指不愿费力的态度，最后扩展到病人与市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slumped figure with no wish to lift a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个垂着肩膀、连手都不想抬的人。

branches.en: A body without eagerness is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 没有热情的身体是日常义项。

branches.en: Refusal to try is the same gap seen in behaviour.
branches.cn: 不愿尝试是同一个空缺在行为上的表现。

branches.en: Patients lacking alertness are the clinical sense.
branches.cn: 缺乏警觉的病人是临床义项。

branches.en: Slack trading is the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 清淡的交易是机构层面的义项。

branches.en: Tiredness and indifference reinforce each other in the word.
branches.cn: 疲倦与漠然在每个义项中彼此加强。

intro.en: Listless is a plain English compound of an old desire noun and a bare negation suffix.
intro.cn: listless 是纯英语复合词，由表示意愿的古名词与表示「无」的后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, and the lack it names has no Latin counterpart of its own.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是英语本族词，它表达的「缺失」并无对应的拉丁词。

items.example: The old noun list lies inside the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 古名词 list 藏在形容词内部。

items.example: Lystan is the reconstructed ancestor.
items.exampleCN: lystan 是重构形式上的祖形。

items.example: The suffix -less negates the noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 否定前面的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms listlessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 listlessly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms listlessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 listlessness。

items.example: Listlessly describes the manner of an act.
items.exampleCN: listlessly 描述动作方式。

items.example: Listlessness names the condition.
items.exampleCN: listlessness 命名这种状态。

items.example: Lust keeps the positive desire of the old word.
items.exampleCN: lust 保留古词中「欲望」的正值。

definition_zh: 字面上的；完全照字面的；逐字的
definition_en: using the most basic or exact meaning of words, without metaphor or exaggeration
core_image: 放大镜贴着书页，只看一个一个字母的原样
scene: 翻译课上，老师提醒大家先弄清字面意思，再考虑修辞。In translation class, the teacher asks us to grasp the literal meaning first and then think about style.
sceneCN: 这里 literal 是「字面上的」（第 01 个义项：照字面而不带比喻义）；句意：翻译课上，老师提醒大家先弄清字面意思，再考虑修辞。

pos.zh: 字面上的；逐字的；完全照字面的

collocations.zh: 并非字面意思；带有比喻
照字面理解的；不会变通的

derivatives.zh: 逐字地；字面上地；口语中常作加强语气用，义为「简直」
字面主义；拘泥字面
与 literal 同源，由拉丁语 littera（字母）派生，义为「读写能力」

senses.title: Following the basic meaning of words
senses.titleCN: 字面上的；按字面理解的
senses.definition: using the ordinary, exact sense of a word rather than a figurative one
senses.definitionCN: 按词语普通而确切的意义理解，而不是比喻义
senses.example: He took my advice in its literal sense.
senses.exampleCN: 他把我建议按字面意思来理解了。
senses.why: The Latin root littera means a letter, so a literal reading stays with the letters themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 littera 意为「字母」，所以字面理解就是紧贴着字母本身读。

senses.title: Word for word
senses.definition: translating or copying each word separately without changing the wording
senses.definitionCN: 把每个词逐一照搬翻译或抄写，而不改写措辞
senses.example: A literal translation of the poem loses its rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的直译会失去节奏。
senses.why: If words are first of all letters, then a word by word version is the most letter-bound kind of translation.
senses.whyCN: 既然词首先是一串字母，那么逐词对照的译法就是最贴紧字母的翻法。

senses.title: Exactly so, though hard to believe
senses.titleCN: 确确实实的（多用于夸张口气）
senses.definition: used to make a description stronger by insisting that what is said is exactly true
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强说法，强调所讲确实如此、并非夸张
senses.example: The hall was filled with a literal wall of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里简直是声浪筑成的一堵墙。
senses.why: By shooting past the literal meaning, a speaker can suggest that the effect was as real as a physical object, though this sense is often playful.
senses.whyCN: 说话人越过字面意、把效果说成实物，就能强调效果之强；不过这一层常带戏谑口气。

intro.en: Literal comes from Latin littera, a letter, through Latin litteralis, of letters.
intro.cn: literal 来自拉丁语 littera（字母），经由 litteralis（与字母有关的）进入英语。

items.en: Littera means a letter of the alphabet.
items.cn: 拉丁语 littera 意为字母表中的一个字母。

items.en: Litteralis means relating to letters or writing.
items.cn: litteralis 意为与字母或书写有关的。

items.en: Litteralis is also used for the exact sense of written words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 litteralis 也指书面词语的确切含义。

items.en: The word enters English as literal, of letters or writing.
items.cn: 该词以 literal 进入英语，意为「与字母或书写有关的」。

items.en: The sense of following the exact wording becomes common.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，「按确切字句理解」的义项流行起来。

items.en: Modern English uses literal for word for word translation and, informally, for colourful exaggeration.
items.cn: 现代英语用 literal 指逐字翻译，口语中又借它作夸张强调。

note.en: Literal sits beside the letter family of literacy and literature, and beside exactness words such as exact, verbatim, and figurative as its opposite.
note.cn: literal 与 literacy、literature 的「字母」词族相邻，也与 exact、verbatim 等「确切」词相邻，反义则有 figurative。

entries.definition: able to read and write
entries.definitionCN: 会读会写的；识字的（同源于拉丁语字母一词）

entries.definition: relating to literature
entries.definitionCN: 文学的（与 literal 同源，只差一个后缀）

entries.definition: written works such as novels and poems
entries.definitionCN: 文学；文学作品（同根名词）

entries.definition: using words in a non literal, imaginative way
entries.definitionCN: 比喻的；借喻的（literal 的反义）

entries.definition: repeating words exactly as they were said or written
entries.definitionCN: 逐字地；一字不差地

entries.definition: completely correct in every detail
entries.definitionCN: 确切的；精确的

normalIntro.en: Literal is built on the Latin word for letter: to read literally is to read only the letters in front of you.
normalIntro.cn: literal 建立在拉丁语「字母」一词上：字面地读，就是只读眼前这些字母。

normal.en: The literal meaning of a word is the plain sense it carries in a dictionary.
normal.cn: literal meaning 就是词典里那种朴素的意思。

normal.en: A literal translation copies words one by one, so it often sounds stiff.
normal.cn: literal translation 逐词照搬，所以常常生硬。

normal.en: In the literal sense means not as a figure of speech.
normal.cn: in the literal sense 表示不是打比方。

normal.en: Briefly means shortly in length, not briefly in time, which is its literal reading.
normal.cn: briefly 按字面指篇幅短，而不是时间短。

normal.en: Compare literal and literary: both come from letter, but literary belongs to books and poetry.
normal.cn: 对比 literal 与 literary：同出自「字母」，但 literary 属于书籍与诗歌。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass pressed flat against a page, seeing only the shapes of letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚放大镜平压在书页上，只看得到字母的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a bicycle slipping and falling on a wet road, a really literal of the Latin word for slipping.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆自行车在湿路上滑了一跤，正是拉丁语「滑倒」一词的字面画面。

abstract.en: Hear someone say the word is meant exactly, like a stamp landing flat on paper.
abstract.cn: 听某人在强调字字属实，像一枚印章平正地落在纸上。

examples.en: The literal meaning of the word is a small room, but here it points to a person.
examples.cn: 这个词的字面意思是小房间，但这里指人。

examples.en: A literal translation of the contract confused the buyer.
examples.cn: 合同的直译让买家看糊涂了。

examples.en: Do not take his joke in its literal sense.
examples.cn: 别把他的玩笑当字面意思来理解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离特柔」——字面理解太死板，读起来又「离」又「特」又「柔」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母）+ -alis（形容词后缀）→ litteralis → 古法语 → 英语 literal，核心义「只盯字母本身」。

sensesIntro.en: Literal begins with the plain sense of words, moves to word by word translation, and slips into an emphatic, half playful usage.
sensesIntro.cn: literal 从词语的朴素字义出发，扩展到逐字翻译，再滑向一种强调而略带戏谑的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass held tightly against a page, reading only the letters.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜紧贴书页，只读字母本身。

branches.en: The plain dictionary sense is the everyday core.
branches.cn: 词典里的朴素意义是日常核心义项。

branches.en: Word for word copying grows out of letter-bound reading.
branches.cn: 逐字照搬的义项由「贴着字母」的阅读方式长出。

branches.en: Insisting that a description is exact turns literal into emphasis.
branches.cn: 强调描述确有其事时，literal 就变成了加强语气。

branches.en: A literal translation is judged by how closely it keeps the original wording.
branches.cn: 直译的好坏取决于它多贴近原文措辞。

branches.en: All three senses share the same refusal of metaphor, exaggeration included.
branches.cn: 三个义项都拒绝比喻，连夸张也一并排除。

intro.en: Literal is a Latin adjective in -alis built on littera, meaning a letter.
intro.cn: literal 是以 littera（字母）为词根、加 -alis 构成的拉丁形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera means a letter, and litteralis means of letters; English keeps both the root and the suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 littera 意为字母，litteralis 意为与字母有关的；英语把词根和后缀都保留了下来。

items.example: Littera gives the letter image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: littera 提供这个词背后的字母意象。

items.example: The suffix -al turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Litteralis is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: litteralis 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Literal keeps the letter-bound sense.
items.exampleCN: literal 保留了「贴着字母」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms literally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 literally。

items.meaning: word for word or without exaggeration
items.example: Literally is the adverb form.
items.exampleCN: literally 是形容词的副词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms literalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 literalism。

items.example: Literalism names a habit of sticking to the letter.
items.exampleCN: literalism 指死守字面的习惯。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.example: Literacy grew from the same letter root through Latin litteratus.
items.exampleCN: literacy 经拉丁语 litteratus 也从「字母」词根长出来。

derivatives.zh: 逐字地；确实地；口语中常作加强语气用
